children.translated_text: The commentary on the <s>Śrīmaitrāyaṇīya Mānavagṛhyasūtra</s> /
First <s>Puruṣa</s> (section) /
First <s>Khaṇḍa</s> (chapter)
Now begins the <s>Mānavagṛhyasūtra</s> /
Oṃ. Beginning from the <s>upanayana</s> (initiation), one should observe the <s>vrata</s> (vow) // ManGS_1,1.1 //
Wearing the garments of a wanderer, with matted hair, following the conduct of a mendicant, carrying a staff with bark — [these are] seven [rules] /
He should wear a girdle of <s>muñja</s> grass, not acting contrary to the <s>ācārya</s> (teacher), doing everything [for the teacher] // ManGS_1,1.2 //

children.text: yadenamupeyāt tadasmai dadyād bahūnāṃ yena saṃyuktaḥ // ManGS_1,1.3 //
children.translated_text: Whatever [the student] would bring to him, that he should give; that by which he is connected with many // ManGS_1,1.3 //
He should not occupy his [teacher's] bed // ManGS_1,1.4 //
He should not lounge about // ManGS_1,1.5 //
He should not mount a chariot // ManGS_1,1.6 //
He should not speak falsehood // ManGS_1,1.7 //
He should not look at a naked woman // ManGS_1,1.8 //
He should not engage in idle conversation for entertainment // ManGS_1,1.9 //
He should not wear anything merely for the sake of pleasure // ManGS_1,1.10 //

children.text: sarvāṇi sāṃ sparśikāni strībhyo varjjayet // ManGS_1,1.11 //
children.translated_text: He should avoid all physical contact with women // ManGS_1,1.11 //

children.text: na madhumāṃse prāśnīyāt kṣāralavaṇe ca // ManGS_1,1.12 //
children.translated_text: He should not eat honey or meat, nor alkaline substances or salt // ManGS_1,1.12 //
He should not bathe [for pleasure] nor apply water [for decoration] // ManGS_1,1.13 //
If he does bathe, he should float in the water like a stick // ManGS_1,1.14 //

children.text: prāgastamayānniṣkramya samidhāvahārerddhariṇyau brahmavarcasakāma iti śrutiḥ // ManGS_1,1.15 //
children.translated_text: Going out before sunset to fetch two fuel-sticks that bring prosperity — 'desiring <s>brahmavarcas</s> (spiritual radiance)' — thus says the <s>śruti</s> (scripture) // ManGS_1,1.15 //

children.text: imaṃ stomamarhata ityagniṃ parisamuhya paryukṣya paristīryaidhosyedhiṣīmahīti samidhamādadhāti, samidasi samedhiṣīmahīti dvitīyām // ManGS_1,1.16 //
children.translated_text: Having swept around the fire, sprinkled water, and strewn [grass], with [the mantra] 'imāṃ stomam arhata' (be worthy of this praise), he places a fuel-stick [saying] 'edhosyedhiṣīmahi' (you are fuel, may we prosper), the second with 'samidasi samedhiṣīmahi' (you are a fuel-stick, may we prosper together) // ManGS_1,1.16 //
He worships with [the verse] 'apo adyānvacāriṣam' (I have today followed the waters) // ManGS_1,1.17 //
That which in the beginning through <s>tapas</s> (austerity), through <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibate studentship), one has approached /

children.text: priyāḥ śrutasya bhūyāsmāyuṣmantaḥ sumedhasa iti mukhaṃ vimṛṣṭe // ManGS_1,1.18 //
children.translated_text: May we be dear, endowed with long life, and of good wisdom through learning — thus he wipes his face // ManGS_1,1.18 //

children.text: bhadraṃ karṇebhiḥ śṛṇuyāma devā iti śrotre abhimṛśati // ManGS_1,1.19 //
children.translated_text: He touches his ears with [the verse] 'bhadraṃ karṇebhiḥ śṛṇuyāma devāḥ' (May we hear what is auspicious with our ears, O gods) // ManGS_1,1.19 //

children.text: bhadraṃ paśyemākṣābhir yajatrā iti cakṣuṣī // ManGS_1,1.20 //
children.translated_text: 'Bhadraṃ paśyemākṣabhir yajatrāḥ' (May we see what is auspicious with our eyes, O worshipful ones) — [he touches] the eyes // ManGS_1,1.20 //

children.text: sthirai raṅgai stuṣṭuvāṃ sastanūbhir vyaśema devahitaṃ yadāyu rityaṅgāni // ManGS_1,1.21 //
children.translated_text: 'Sthirair aṅgais tuṣṭuvāṃsas tanūbhiḥ vyaśema devahitaṃ yad āyuḥ' (With firm limbs and bodies, praising, may we attain the life that is ordained by the gods) — [he touches] the limbs // ManGS_1,1.21 //

children.text: iha dhṛtiriha svadhṛtiriti hṛdayadeśamārabhya japati // ManGS_1,1.22 //
children.translated_text: He murmurs touching the region of the heart with 'iha dhṛtiḥ iha svadhṛtiḥ' (here is steadfastness, here is self-support) // ManGS_1,1.22 //
He touches the earth with 'rucaṃ no dhehi' (bestow splendor upon us) // ManGS_1,1.23 //
The triple lifespan of <s>Jamadagni</s>, the triple lifespan of <s>Kaśyapa</s>, the triple lifespan of <s>Agastya</s> /

children.text: yaddevānāṃ tryāyuṣaṃ tanme astu tryāyuṣamiti bhasmānāṅgāni saṃspṛśyāpohiṣṭhīyābhirmārjāyate // ManGS_1,1.24 //
children.translated_text: That which is the triple lifespan of the gods, may that be mine — with 'tryāyuṣam' (triple lifespan), having touched the limbs with ashes, he purifies himself with the 'āpo hiṣṭha' (you are the foremost of waters) verses // ManGS_1,1.24 //
Thus ends the first <s>khaṇḍa</s> (chapter) //1//
Second <s>khaṇḍa</s> (chapter) /
Oṃ. Now he performs the <s>sandhyā</s> (twilight worship) // ManGS_1,2.1 //

children.text: prāgastamayānniṣkramyottarato grāmasya purastādvā śucau deśe niṣedyopaspṛśyāpāmañjaliṃpūrayitvā pradakṣiṇamāvṛtya āyāhiviraje devyakṣare brahmasaṃmite /
children.translated_text: Going out before sunset, to the north of the village or to the east, sitting in a clean place, having sipped water, filling the cupped hands with water, turning to the right,

children.text: gāyatrīṃ chandasāṃ mātaridaṃ brahma juṣasva me ' ityāvāhayati // ManGS_1,2.2 //
children.translated_text: He invokes [<s>Gāyatrī</s>] with 'āyāhi viraje devyakṣare brahmasaṃmite / gāyatrīṃ chandasāṃ mātaridaṃ brahma juṣasva me' (Come, O divine <s>Virāj</s>, imperishable one, conforming to <s>Brahman</s>; O <s>Gāyatrī</s>, mother of metres, accept this <s>Brahman</s> for me) // ManGS_1,2.2 //

children.text: ādyojo 'sīti japitvā kaste yunaktīti yojayitvoṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svastatsaviturityaṣṭau kṛtvaḥ prayuṅkta ityāmnātāḥ kāmā ādevo yātīti triṣṭubhaṃ rājavanyasya yuñjata iti jagatiṃ vaiśamya // ManGS_1,2.3 //
children.translated_text: Having recited 'ādyojaḥ asi' (you are the primordial vigor), and having yoked with 'kaḥ te yunakti' (who yokes you), he employs 'Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svas tat savitur' eight times — thus it is taught; the desires with 'ādevo yāti'; the <s>triṣṭubh</s> metre for the <s>rājanya</s> (warrior) with 'yuñjata'; and the <s>jagatī</s> metre for the <s>vaiśya</s> // ManGS_1,2.3 //

children.text: udutyaṃ jātavedasamiti dve nigadya kaste vimuñjatīti vimucyodakāñjalimutsṛjati // ManGS_1,2.4 //
children.translated_text: Having recited the two [verses] 'ud u tyaṃ jātavedasam' (up rises <s>Jātavedas</s>), and having released with 'kaḥ te vimuñcati' (who releases you), he pours out a handful of water // ManGS_1,2.4 //
Similarly in the morning, standing // ManGS_1,2.5 //

children.text: etena dharmeṇa dvādaśacaturviṃśatiṃ ṣaṭtriśatamaṣṭācatvāriṃ śataṃ vā varṣāṇi yo brāhmaṇo rājanyo vaiśyo vā drahmacaryaṃ carati muṇḍaḥ śikhājaṭaḥ sarvajaṭo vā malajñurabalaḥ kṛśaḥ snātvā sa sarvaṃ vindate yatkiṃcinmanasecchatīti // ManGS_1,2.6 //
children.translated_text: By this observance, a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, <s>rājanya</s> (warrior), or <s>vaiśya</s> who practices <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibate studentship) for twelve, twenty-four, thirty-six, or forty-eight years — whether shaven, wearing a topknot, with matted locks, or with fully matted hair — soiled, without ornaments, thin — having bathed, he obtains whatever his mind desires // ManGS_1,2.6 //
By this observance, one studies well // ManGS_1,2.7 //
Having understood the meanings in the Vedic texts, when about to take the ritual bath, he should have a cow prepared [as a gift] // ManGS_1,2.8 //
He should honor the <s>ācārya</s> (teacher); [then he becomes] a <s>śrotriya</s> (learned in the Vedas) // ManGS_1,2.9 //

children.text: anyo vedapāṭhī na tasya snānam // ManGS_1,2.10 //
children.translated_text: Another who merely recites the <s>Veda</s> [without understanding] — for him there is no [ritual] bath [of completion] // ManGS_1,2.10 //

children.text: āpo hiṣṭheti tisṛbhirhiraṇyavarṇāḥ śucaya iti dvābhyāṃ snātvāhate vāsasī paridhatte // ManGS_1,2.11 //
children.translated_text: Having bathed with the three [verses] 'āpo hiṣṭha' (you are the foremost of waters) and the two 'hiraṇyavarṇāḥ śucayaḥ' (golden-colored, pure), he puts on a pair of fresh garments // ManGS_1,2.11 //

children.text: vasvasi vasumantaṃ mā kuru sauvarcasāya mā tejase brahmavarcasāya paridadhāmīti paridadhāti // ManGS_1,2.12 //
children.translated_text: He puts on [the garment saying] 'vasv asi vasumantaṃ mā kuru sauvarcasāya mā tejase brahmavarcasāya paridadhāmi' (you are wealth; make me wealthy, for glory, for radiance, for <s>brahmavarcas</s> — I put you on) // ManGS_1,2.12 //

children.text: yathā dyauśca pṛthivī ca na bibhīto na riṣyataḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as heaven and earth neither fear nor are injured /

children.text: evaṃ me prāṇa mā riṣa ityāṅkte // ManGS_1,2.13 //
children.translated_text: Thus, O my <s>prāṇa</s> (life-breath), may I not be injured — so he anoints himself // ManGS_1,2.13 //
He ties on gold [ornament] // ManGS_1,2.14 //

children.text: chatraṃ dhārayate daṇḍaṃ mālāṃ gandham // ManGS_1,2.15 //
children.translated_text: He carries an umbrella, a staff, a garland, and fragrant paste // ManGS_1,2.15 //

children.text: pratiṣṭhe sthodaivate dyāvāpṛthivī mā mā saṃtāptamityupānahau // ManGS_1,2.16 //
children.translated_text: 'You are firmly established; your deities are heaven and earth; do not burn me' — [thus he puts on] shoes // ManGS_1,2.16 //

children.text: dvivastro 'ta urdhvaṃ bhavati tasmācchobhanaṃ vāso bhartavyamiti śrutiḥ // ManGS_1,2.17 //
children.translated_text: From that point onward he wears two garments; therefore one should wear a fine garment — thus says the <s>śruti</s> (scripture) // ManGS_1,2.17 //
Having taken leave of the elders and the kinsmen of the elders, he should go to his own home // ManGS_1,2.18 //

children.text: pratiṣiddhamaparayā dvārā niṣkramaṇaṃ malavadvāsasā saha saṃvastraṇaṃ rajaḥ sunāsinyā saha śayyā gurorduruktavacanamasthāne śayanaṃ smayanaṃ saraṇaṃ sthānaṃ yānaṃ gānaṃ tasya cekṣaṇam // ManGS_1,2.19 //
children.translated_text: The following are prohibited: exiting through the back door; sleeping together with one wearing soiled garments; sharing a bed with a menstruating woman; speaking harsh words to the teacher; sleeping, smiling, running, standing, riding, or singing in an improper place; and looking at such [improper things] // ManGS_1,2.19 //
On the full moon or new moon day, he should sacrifice with a <s>vaiśvadeva</s> animal offering to <s>Agni</s> // ManGS_1,2.20 //

children.text: tasya pavirbhakṣayitvā yathāsukhamata ūrdhvaṃ madhumāṃse prāśnīyātkṣāralavaṇe ca // ManGS_1,2.21 //
children.translated_text: Having tasted the sacrificial cake thereof, from that point onward he may eat honey and meat, and alkaline substances and salt as he pleases // ManGS_1,2.21 //
Thus ends the second <s>khaṇḍa</s> (chapter) //
Third <s>khaṇḍa</s> (chapter) /
If one who knows thus should [miss the sunrise] or [miss the sunset], upon waking he should recite:
May my faculties return to me again, may my life return again, may my fortune return again,

children.text: punardraviṇā maitu māṃ punarvāhyaṇa maitu mām
children.translated_text: May my wealth come to me again, may <s>Brahman</s> come to me again,
Now, just as these <s>dhiṣṇya</s> (fire-hearths) and fires
Arrange themselves in their proper places — [thus one recites when the sun has] risen [before one's waking] // ManGS_1,3.1 //

children.text: punarmātmā punarāyuraitu punaḥ prāṇaḥ punarākūtiraitu vaiśvānaro vāvṛdhāno vareṇāntastiṣṭhato me mano amṛtasya ketuḥ ityabhyasta mitaḥ // ManGS_1,3.2 //
children.translated_text: 'May my self return again, may my life return, may my breath return, may my intention return; <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, increasing through excellence, standing within me — the beacon of the immortal, my mind' — [this he recites when the sun has] set [before his notice] // ManGS_1,3.2 //
Or one may recite both [mantras] at sunrise, or both at sunset // ManGS_1,3.3 //

children.text: yadyācaraṇīyānvācaredanākrośedabhojyasyavānna maśnīyādakṣi vāspandetkarṇo vākrośedagniṃ vā citimārohetsmaśānaṃ vā gacchedyupaṃ vospṛśedretaso vā skandedetābhyāmeva mantrābhyāmāhutirjuhuyādapi vājyalipte samidhe vādadhyādapi vā mantrāveva japet // ManGS_1,3.4 //
children.translated_text: If he should commit a transgression of conduct, or abuse someone, or eat food of one whose food should not be eaten, or if his eye should twitch, or his ear should ring, or if he should mount a funeral pyre, or go to a cremation ground, or touch a sacrificial post, or have an emission of semen — with these two <s>mantras</s> he should offer an <s>āhuti</s> (oblation), or he should place fuel-sticks smeared with ghee, or he should simply recite the two <s>mantras</s> // ManGS_1,3.4 //
Thus [is the expiation for] a gross transgression of <s>dharma</s> // ManGS_1,3.5 //

children.text: sthūle veṣaṇayā viharedavastro lomatvagācchādo 'gnimārohetsaṃgrāme vā dhātayedapi vāgnimindhānaṃ tapasā'tmānamupayojayīta // ManGS_1,3.6 //
children.translated_text: For a gross [transgression], he should wander with a yoke; or unclothed, covered with hair or skin, he should ascend the fire, or fight in battle, or kindle the fire, devoting himself to <s>tapas</s> (austerity) // ManGS_1,3.6 //
Thus ends the third <s>khaṇḍa</s> (chapter)
Fourth <s>khaṇḍa</s> (chapter)
During the rainy season, on [the day of the constellation] <s>Śravaṇa</s>, he commences the <s>svādhyāya</s> (Vedic study) // ManGS_1,4.1 //
He offers oblations —

children.text:
apvānāmāsi tasyāstejoṣṭraṃ gamayem /
ahamiddhi pituḥ parimedhāmṛtasya jagrabha sūrya ivājani svāhā /
children.translated_text: 'You are [the deity] of the waters; may I attain your splendor and glory / I have indeed grasped the wisdom of my father, the immortal; I was born like <s>Sūrya</s> (the Sun), <s>svāhā</s>' /
'You are named <s>Sarasvatī</s>; you are named <s>Sarasvān</s>' /
'You are named <s>Yukti</s> (connection); you are named <s>Yoga</s> (union)' /
'You are named <s>Mati</s> (thought); you are named <s>Manas</s> (mind)' //
'May I attain your splendor and glory' /
'May I attain that splendor and glory' — this is appended everywhere // ManGS_1,4.2 //

children.text: yuje svāhā prayuje svāhodyujesvāhetyetairattevāsināṃ yogamicchanniti // ManGS_1,4.3 //
children.translated_text: 'I yoke, <s>svāhā</s>; I employ, <s>svāhā</s>; I unyoke, <s>svāhā</s>' — with these [mantras, he offers oblations] desiring the union of the resident students // ManGS_1,4.3 //
Before the <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s> (oblation for the correction of errors), then he recites /

children.text: ṛtaṃ vadiṣyāmi satyaṃ vadiṣyāmi tanmāmavatu tadvaktāramavatvavatu mā bhavatu vaktāram /
children.translated_text: 'I shall speak what is right; I shall speak what is true. May that protect me; may that protect the speaker. May it protect me; may it protect the speaker' /

children.text: vāṅ me manasi pratiṣṭhinā, mano me vaici pratiṣṭhitamāvirāyurmayi dhehi vedasya vāṇīḥ stha /
children.translated_text: 'May my speech be established in my mind; may my mind be established in my speech. May you grant me long life. You are the utterances of the <s>Veda</s>' /
'Oṃ <s>bhūḥ bhuvaḥ svaḥ tat savituḥ</s>' [the <s>Gāyatrī</s>] // ManGS_1,4.4 //
Holding <s>darbha</s> (sacred grass) in hand, he recites the <s>Sāvitrī</s> three times /
And the first three <s>anuvākas</s> (sections) /
And 'ko vā yunakti' (who indeed yokes) /
And 'upākurmahe 'dhyāyān upatisṭhantu chandāṃsi' (we commence; may the metres attend upon the lessons) // ManGS_1,4.5 //

children.text: tasyānadhyāyāḥ samūhanvāto valīkakṣāraprabhṛti varṣaṃ na vidyotamāne na stanayatīti śrutirākālikaṃ devatumulaṃ vidyuddhanvolkātyakṣarāḥ śabdāḥ /
children.translated_text: The days on which study is prohibited: when wind sweeps up [debris], from the appearance of lightning and thunderclouds onwards, rain, as long as there is lightning and thunder — thus says the <s>śruti</s>; occasional [prohibitions include] divine tumult, lightning, meteors, and loud sounds /
Others [are prohibited] by custom // ManGS_1,4.6 //
Having studied for four and a half months, he concludes; or for five and a half months according to some // ManGS_1,4.7 //

children.text: atha japati ṛta mavādiṣaṃ tanmāvīt ttadvaktāramāvīdāvīnmāmāvīdvaktāram /
children.translated_text: Then he recites: 'I have spoken what is right; that has protected me; that protected the speaker; it protected me; it protected the speaker' /

children.text: vādh me manasi pratiṣṭhitā mano me vāci pratiṣṭhitaṃ māvirāyur mayi dhehi /
children.translated_text: 'My speech is established in my mind; my mind is established in my speech. May you grant me long life' /
'You are the utterances of the <s>Veda</s>' /
'Oṃ <s>bhūḥ bhuvaḥ svaḥ tat savituḥ</s>' [the <s>Gāyatrī</s>] // ManGS_1,4.8 //
Holding <s>darbha</s> (sacred grass) in hand, he recites the <s>Sāvitrī</s> three times /

children.text: trīṃścādito 'muvākān ko vo vimuñcatīti vimucyotsṛjāmahedhyāyānpratīśvasantu chandāsīti ca // ManGS_1,4.9 //
children.translated_text: And the first three <s>anuvākas</s>; 'ko vo vimuñcati' (who releases you); having released and concluded — 'utsṛjāmahe 'dhyāyān pratīśvasantu chandāṃsi' (we conclude; may the metres breathe again) // ManGS_1,4.9 //

children.text: pratipadaṃ pakṣiṇīṃ rātrīṃ nādhīyīta nāta ūrdhvamabhreṣu // ManGS_1,4.10 //
children.translated_text: On the first day of [each] fortnight, and on nights containing a [full] <s>pakṣa</s> (fortnight), one should not study; nor from that point onward when there are clouds // ManGS_1,4.10 //
[Study is prohibited] at the occasional [occurrence of] lightning, thunder, and rain // ManGS_1,4.11 //

The <s>gonāma</s> [texts], <s>mantra-brāhmaṇa</s>, <s>kalpayitṛ</s>, <s>medha</s>, <s>mahāvrata</s>, <s>aṣṭāpadī</s>, and <s>vaiṣuvatāni</s> should be studied during the day; the <s>vaiṣuvata</s> [texts] with wet hands // ManGS_1,4.12 //

children.text: rudānna naktaṃ na bhuktā na grāme // ManGS_1,4.13 //
children.translated_text: One should not [study] while weeping, nor at night, nor after eating, nor in the village // ManGS_1,4.13 //

children.text: śukriyasya pravargyakalpe niyamo vyākhyātastrayoviṃśaṃ tu saṃmīlya // ManGS_1,4.14 //
children.translated_text: The observance in the <s>pravargya</s> ritual of <s>Śukriya</s> is explained [elsewhere]; but the twenty-third [section] is to be recited with closed eyes // ManGS_1,4.14 //

children.text: gavāṃ tu na sakāśe gonāmāni gārbhiṇīnāmasakāśe 'ṣṭāpadīṃreto mūtramiti ca // ManGS_1,4.15 //
children.translated_text: The <s>gonāma</s> [texts] should not [be studied] in the presence of cows; the <s>aṣṭāpadī</s> should not [be studied] in the presence of pregnant women; and [texts mentioning] semen and urine [should also not be studied in their presence] // ManGS_1,4.15 //

children.text: śunīśīryasya ca saurye cakṣuṣkāmasya cakṣurno dhehi cakṣuṣa iti sūryo 'po 'vagāhata iti ca ādityasairyayāmyāni ṣaḍṛcāni divādhīyīta // ManGS_1,4.16 //
children.translated_text: The <s>cakṣuṣkāma</s> (desiring sight) [verses] of <s>Śunīśīra</s>, and the solar [hymns] — 'cakṣur no dhehi cakṣuṣaḥ' (bestow sight upon our sight) and 'sūryo 'po 'vagāhata' (the sun plunged into the waters) — and the six <s>ādityasairya</s> verses of <s>Yama</s> should be studied during the day // ManGS_1,4.16 //
After commencing and after concluding [study], [there is a pause of] three days; five nights according to some // ManGS_1,4.17 //
At the beginning and completion of <s>Veda</s> [study], [the pause lasts] until the proper time // ManGS_1,4.18 //
Thus ends the fourth <s>khaṇḍa</s> (chapter) /
Fifth <s>khaṇḍa</s> (chapter)
Now we shall explain the intermediate ritual // ManGS_1,5.1 //

children.text: darbhamayaṃ vāsaḥ paridhāyacamyāpāṃ naptra iti tīre japitvāpo 'vagāhya oṃbhūrbhuvaḥ svastatsavituriti // ManGS_1,5.2 //
children.translated_text: Having put on a garment made of <s>darbha</s> grass and having sipped water, after reciting 'apāṃ naptrā' (O son of the waters) on the bank, entering the water, [he recites] 'Oṃ <s>bhūḥ bhuvaḥ svaḥ tat savituḥ</s>' // ManGS_1,5.2 //
Holding <s>darbha</s> grass in hand, he recites the <s>Sāvitrī</s> three times, and the first three <s>anuvākas</s> // ManGS_1,5.3 //

children.text: āpo devīrhaviṣmatīrimā nigrābhyo stha mahitrīṇāmavo 'stu agnerarāyurasi devī rāpo apāṃ napāddevīrāpo madhumatīragnaye svāhā rātrīṃ rātrīmityaṣṭau // ManGS_1,5.4 //
children.translated_text: [He recites] eight [mantras]: 'āpo devīḥ haviṣmatīḥ' (O divine waters, rich in oblations), 'imā nigrābhyaḥ stha' (you are for these offerings), 'mahitrīṇāṃ avaḥ astu' (may there be protection of the great ones), 'agner arāyuḥ asi' (you are the gift of <s>Agni</s>), 'devīḥ āpaḥ' (O divine waters), 'apāṃ napāt' (O son of the waters), 'devīḥ āpo madhumatīḥ' (O divine waters, rich in honey), 'agnaye svāhā rātrīṃ rātrīm' (to <s>Agni</s>, svāhā, night after night) // ManGS_1,5.4 //

children.text: yā oṣadhayaḥ samānyāyanti punantu mā pitaro 'gnermanve saśevṛdhamadhidhāḥ kayā naścitra ābhuvadūtīti tisraḥ // ManGS_1,5.5 //
children.translated_text: [He recites] three [mantras]: 'yā oṣadhayaḥ samānyā' (those herbs that are equal), 'yanti' (they go), 'punantu mā pitaraḥ' (may the ancestors purify me), 'agner manve saśe vṛdham adhidhāḥ' (you who have placed upon <s>Agni</s> the growing offering), 'kayā naś citrā ābhuvad ūtī' (with what wonderful aid) // ManGS_1,5.5 //

children.text: tacchaṃyorā vṛṇīmaha iti mārjayitvā vāsāṃsyutsṛjāyācāryānpitṛdharmeṇa tarpayanti // ManGS_1,5.6 //
children.translated_text: Having purified with 'tac chaṃyor āvṛṇīmahe' (we choose that which is auspicious and beneficial), they release the garments and gratify the <s>ācāryas</s> (teachers) according to the rites for ancestors // ManGS_1,5.6 //
The remainder is explained according to the <s>śrāddha</s> (ancestral offering) ritual // ManGS_1,5.7 //
Thus ends the fifth <s>khaṇḍa</s> (chapter) /
Sixth <s>khaṇḍa</s> (chapter) /
Now they establish the [sacred] fire // ManGS_1,6.1 //

children.text: uttarato grāmasya purastādvā śucau deśe vedyākṛtiṃ kṛtvāhavanīyasthāne saptacchandāṃsi pratiṣṭhāpya viṣṭharā darbhamuṣṭhīnvā dakṣiṇāgnisthāne praugākṛtiṃ kauśitaṃ khātvā paścādutkaramapāṃ pūrayitvā
children.translated_text: To the north of the village or to the east, in a clean place, having made an altar-shaped [area], having established the seven metres at the <s>āhavanīya</s> (offering fire) place, [having spread] bundles of <s>darbha</s> grass, having dug a wedge-shaped pit at the <s>dakṣiṇāgni</s> (southern fire) place in the <s>kauśita</s> style, having filled [the pit] with water from the mound behind it,

children.text: gārhapatyasthāne 'gniṃ praṇīya yuñjānaḥ prathamaṃ mana ityaṣṭau dutvā /
children.translated_text: Having brought the fire to the <s>gārhapatya</s> (household fire) place, and having offered eight [oblations] with 'yuñjānaḥ prathamaṃ manaḥ' (yoking the mind first) /

children.text: ñakūtamagniṃ prayujaṃ svāheti ṣaḍ juhoti viśvo devasya netu riti saptamīm // ManGS_1,6.2 //
children.translated_text: He offers six oblations with 'ākūtam agniṃ prayujaṃ svāhā' (intention, fire, employment, svāhā) and a seventh with 'viśvo devasya netuḥ' (of the universal god, the leader) // ManGS_1,6.2 //

children.text: yajñiyānāṃ samidhāṃ trīṃ strīn samitpūlānupakalpya prāksviṣṭakṛtastiṣṭhanto vyāhṛtipūrvakaṃ khaṇḍilasyādītastribhi ranuvākairekaikena svāhākārāntābhirādadhati // ManGS_1,6.3 //
children.translated_text: Having prepared three bundles of three fuel-sticks each from sacrificial trees, before the <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s> oblation, standing, preceded by the <s>vyāhṛtis</s> (sacred utterances), with three <s>anuvākas</s> beginning from <s>Khaṇḍila</s>, they place [the fuel-sticks] one by one, each ending with <s>svāhā</s> // ManGS_1,6.3 //

children.text: āpodiṣṭīyābhiḥ kausitān mārjayitvā dhānābhir brābmaṇānsvasti vācayanti dhānābhir brāhmaṇānsvasti vācayanti // ManGS_1,6.4 //
children.translated_text: Having purified the <s>kauśita</s> [pit] with the 'āpo diṣṭīya' verses, they have the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> pronounce blessings with parched grains; they have the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> pronounce blessings with parched grains // ManGS_1,6.4 //
Thus in the <s>Mānava</s> [sūtra], the sixth <s>khaṇḍa</s> (chapter) //6//
Seventh <s>khaṇḍa</s> (chapter)
Now, those who are worthy of the <s>upaniṣad</s> (secret teaching) /

children.text: brahmacārī sucariti medhāvī karmakṛddhanadaḥ priyo vidhāṃ vā vidyāyānveṣyan // ManGS_1,7.1 //
children.translated_text: A <s>brahmacārī</s> (celibate student) who is well-conducted, intelligent, active in duties, generous, and dear — or one seeking knowledge and learning // ManGS_1,7.1 //
These are the qualifications for [receiving] <s>Brahman</s> (sacred knowledge) // ManGS_1,7.2 //
He finds a wife // ManGS_1,7.3 //
He should choose [a bride born under the constellations] <s>Kṛttikā</s>, <s>Svāti</s>, or the earlier ones // ManGS_1,7.4 //

children.text: rohiṇīmṛgaśiraḥ śravaṇāśraviṣṭhottarāṇītyupayame tathodvāhe yadvā puṇyoktam // ManGS_1,7.5 //
children.translated_text: <s>Rohiṇī</s>, <s>Mṛgaśiras</s>, <s>Śravaṇā</s>, <s>Śraviṣṭhā</s>, and the <s>Uttarā</s> [constellations] — for the betrothal and likewise for the wedding; or whatever is declared auspicious // ManGS_1,7.5 //

children.text: pañca vivāhakārakāṇi bhavanti vittaṃ rūpaṃ vidyā prajñā bāndhava iti // ManGS_1,7.6 //
children.translated_text: There are five qualifications for marriage: wealth, beauty, learning, wisdom, and family // ManGS_1,7.6 //

children.text: ekālābhe vittaṃ visṛjed dvitīyālābhe rūpaṃ tṛtīyālābhe vidyāṃ prajñāyāṃ bāndhava iti ca vivahante // ManGS_1,7.7 //
children.translated_text: When the first [quality] is unattainable, one should forgo wealth; when the second is unattainable, [forgo] beauty; when the third is unattainable, [forgo] learning; and they marry for the sake of offspring and kinship.

children.text: bandhumatīṃ kanyāmaspṛṣṭamaithunā samānavarṇāsamānapravarāṃ yavīyasīṃ nagnikāṃ śreṣṭhām // ManGS_1,7.8 //
children.translated_text: One should [choose] a maiden who has relatives, who has not been touched by sexual intercourse, of the same <s>varṇa</s> (class) but different <s>pravara</s> (lineage), younger [than the groom], a <s>nagnikā</s> (pre-pubescent girl) — such is the best.

children.text: vijñānamasyāḥ kuryādaṣṭau loṣṭhānāharesītā- loṣṭhaṃ vediloṣṭhaṃ dūrvāloṣṭhaṃ gomayaloṣṭhaṃ phalavato vṛkṣasyadhastālloṣṭhaṃ śmaśānaloṣṭha madhvaloṣṭhabhirīṇaloṣṭhamiti // ManGS_1,7.9 //
children.translated_text: One should perform a test of her: one should bring eight clods — a clod from a plowed field, a clod from a <s>vedi</s> (sacrificial altar), a clod with <s>dūrvā</s> grass, a clod of cow-dung, a clod from beneath a fruit-bearing tree, a clod from a cremation ground, a clod from a road, and a clod from barren land.

children.text: devāgāre sthāpayitvātha kanyāṃ grāhayet yadi smaśānaloṣṭhaṃ gṛhṇīyādadhvaloṣṭhabhiriṇaloṣṭhaṃ vā no payamet // ManGS_1,7.10 //
children.translated_text: Having placed [these] in a temple, one should then have the maiden pick [one]; if she picks the cremation-ground clod, or the road clod, or the barren-land clod, one should not marry her.

children.text: saṃjuṣṭāṃ dharmeṇopayaccheta brāhmeṇa śaulkena vā // ManGS_1,7.11 //
children.translated_text: One who is approved should be married by the <s>Brāhma</s> (Brahma form of marriage) rite, or by the <s>śaulka</s> (bride-price) form.

children.text: śatamiti rathaṃ dadyāt gomithunaṃ vā // ManGS_1,7.12 //
children.translated_text: As the 'hundred,' one should give a chariot, or a pair of cattle.
Thus ends the seventh section.
Eighth section.
To the west of the fire, one should arrange four seats.

children.text: teṣūpaviśanti purastatpratyaṅmukho dātā paścātprāṅmukhaḥ pratigrahītā dāturuttarataḥ pratyaṅmukhī kanyā dakṣiṇata udaṅmukho mantrakāraḥ // ManGS_1,8.2 //
children.translated_text: On these they sit: in front, facing west, the giver; behind, facing east, the receiver; to the north of the giver, facing west, the maiden; to the south, facing north, the <s>mantrakāra</s> (reciter of mantras).

children.text: teṣāṃ madhye prāk tūlāndarbhānastīryā kāṃsyamakṣatodakena pūrayitvā avidhavāsmai prayacchati // ManGS_1,8.3 //
children.translated_text: In the middle of these, having spread <s>darbha</s> grass with the tips facing east and their ends [like] cotton, having filled a bronze [vessel] with <s>akṣata</s> (unbroken rice) and water, a non-widowed woman hands it [to the giver].
Therein [is placed] gold.
He announces the eight auspicious [items].

children.text: maṅgalyānyuktā dadāmi pratigṛhṇāmīti trirbrahmadeyā pitā bhrātā vā dadyat // ManGS_1,8.6 //
children.translated_text: Having declared the auspicious items, 'I give,' 'I accept' — three times. In the <s>Brahmadeya</s> (gift of Brahmā) form, the father or brother should give.

children.text: sahiraṇyānañjalīnāvapati dhanāya tvetidātā putrebhyastveti pratigrahītā tasmai pratyāvapati // ManGS_1,8.7 //
children.translated_text: He pours handfuls containing gold: the giver [saying] 'for wealth,' the receiver pours back [saying] 'for sons.'
Having exchanged four times, he gives [her].

children.text: sāvitreṇa kanyāṃ pratigṛhya prajāpataya iti ca ka idaṃ kasmā adāditi sarvatrānuṣajati kāmaitatta itiyantam // ManGS_1,8.9 //
children.translated_text: Having received the maiden with the <s>Sāvitrī</s> [verse] and [the verse] 'to <s>Prajāpati</s>,' and 'Who gave this? To whom did he give?' — he appends [this formula] everywhere, up to 'desire [prompted] this.'

children.text: samānā vā ākūtānīti saha japantyāntādanuvākasya // ManGS_1,8.10 //
children.translated_text: They recite together 'May our intentions be united' up to the end of the <s>anuvāka</s> (section).

children.text: khe rathasya khe nasaḥ yugasya śatakrato apālamindrastriḥ pūrtyavakṛṇotsūryatvaca miti tenodakāṃsyena kanyāmabhiṣiñcet // ManGS_1,8.11 //
children.translated_text: With [the verse] 'In the nave of the chariot, in the nave of the nose, of the yoke — O <s>Śatakratu</s>, <s>Indra</s> thrice transformed <s>Apalā</s>, removing [her] skin like that of <s>Sūrya</s>' — with that, using the bronze vessel with water, he should sprinkle the maiden.
Thus ends the eighth section.
Ninth section.

children.text: ṣaḍadhyārhā bhavantyṛtvigācāryo vivāhyo rājā snātakaḥ priyaśceti // ManGS_1,9.1 //
children.translated_text: Six [persons] are worthy of [the <s>madhuparka</s> (honey-mixture) reception]: the <s>ṛtvij</s> (priest), the <s>ācārya</s> (teacher), the bridegroom, the king, the <s>snātaka</s> (one who has completed his studies), and a dear one.
Or, those who are not connected with a [ritual] occasion, one should honor after the lapse of a year.
Those connected with an occasion are the performers [of the rite] and the invited assessors.
One should not accept the <s>arghya</s> (guest offering) while both parents are alive — thus says the <s>śruti</s> (revealed scripture); alternatively, one may accept it.
Then they honor him.

children.text: kāṃsye camase vā dadhi madhu cānīya varṣīyasā pidhāyācamanīyaprathamaiḥ pratipadyante // ManGS_1,9.6 //
children.translated_text: Having brought curds and honey in a bronze vessel or a <s>camasa</s> (wooden cup), covering it with [a vessel] of larger size, they present [it] with the <s>ācamanīya</s> (sipping water) first.

children.text: virājo dohosi virājo dohosi virājo dohamaśīya mayi dohaḥ padyāyai virājaḥ kalpatāmityekaika māhrimāṇaṃ pratīkṣate // ManGS_1,9.7 //
children.translated_text: With 'You are the milking of <s>Virāj</s>, you are the milking of <s>Virāj</s>, may I partake of the milking of <s>Virāj</s>; may the milking of <s>Virāj</s> come to me for nourishment' — one waits for each [offering] as it is being brought.

children.text: sāvitreṇa viṣṭaraṃ pratigṛhya ahaṃ varṣma sadṛśānāmudyatāmiva sūryaḥ idaṃ tamabhitiṣṭhāmi yo mā kaścābhidāsatīti japati // ManGS_1,9.8 //
children.translated_text: Having received the grass seat with the <s>Sāvitrī</s> [verse], he recites: 'I am the summit among my equals, like the sun risen; I overcome him who assails me.'
The <s>ācārya</s> (teacher) addresses the throne with 'You are the support of the kingdom.'
With 'May no harm [come to you],' he draws the grass seat beneath, at the feet, from below.

children.text: viṣṭara āsīnāyai kaikaṃ triḥ prāha // ManGS_1,9.11 //
children.translated_text: To the one seated on the grass seat, he announces each [item] three times.

children.text: naiva bho ityāha nama ārṣeyāyeti śrutiḥ spṛśatyarghyam // ManGS_1,9.12 //
children.translated_text: He says 'Indeed, sir' and 'Homage to the one of [your] lineage' — [this is] the <s>śruti</s> (scriptural rule); he touches the <s>arghya</s> (guest-water offering).

children.text: pādyena pādau prakṣālya sāvitreṇa madhuparkaṃ pratigṛhya pratiṣṭhāpyavasāyya namo rudrāya pātrasade namo rudrāya pātrasada iti prādeśenādhyadhi pratidiśaṃ pradakṣiṇaṃ
children.translated_text: Having washed the feet with the foot-water, having received the <s>madhuparka</s> (honey-mixture) with the <s>Sāvitrī</s> [verse], having set it down and concluded, [saying] 'Homage to <s>Rudra</s> who presides over the vessel, homage to <s>Rudra</s> who presides over the vessel,' with a span-measure, in each direction, clockwise,
he dedicates [it] in all directions.

children.text: madhuvātā ṛtāyata iti tisṛbhiraṅgulyā pradakṣiṇaṃ pratyṛcaṃ trirāyauti // ManGS_1,9.14 //
children.translated_text: With the three [verses] beginning 'The winds blow sweetness for the righteous,' with the finger, clockwise, for each verse three times, he stirs [the mixture].
With 'You are the immortal underlayer,' he makes the underlayer.

children.text: satyaṃ yaśaḥ śrīrmayi śrīḥśrayatāmiti madhuparkaṃ triḥ prāśnāti // ManGS_1,9.16 //
children.translated_text: With 'Truth, glory, splendor — may splendor rest in me,' he eats the <s>madhuparka</s> (honey-mixture) three times.
With 'You are the immortal covering,' he sips water (<s>ācamana</s>).
He gives the remainder to a friend.
He says 'You are' to the hand, and announces the cow.

children.text: hato me pāpmānaṃ me hata oṃkuruta iti preṣyati // ManGS_1,9.20 //
children.translated_text: He commands: 'Slay my sin, slay it for me, make the exclamation <s>oṃ</s>.'
He feeds four <s>brāhmaṇas</s> of different <s>gotras</s> (lineages).

children.text: paśvaṅgaṃ pāyasaṃ vā kārayennāmāṃso madhuparka iti śrutiḥ // ManGS_1,9.22 //
children.translated_text: He should prepare a limb of an animal, or rice-milk; 'the <s>madhuparka</s> should not be without meat' — thus says the <s>śruti</s> (scripture).

children.text: yadyutsṛjenmātā rudrāṇāṃ duhitā vasūnāṃ svasādityānāmamṛtasya nābhiḥ /
children.translated_text: If one should release [the cow]: 'Mother of the <s>Rudras</s>, daughter of the <s>Vasus</s>, sister of the <s>Ādityas</s>, navel of immortality,

children.text: pranuvocaṃ cikituṣe janāya māgā manāgā maditiṃ vaṅiṣṭa /
children.translated_text: I have spoken to the knowing people: do not slay the guiltless [cow], [she who is] <s>Aditi</s> herself.'
'<s>Bhūr bhuvaḥ svar</s> (earth, atmosphere, heaven) — om, release her; let her eat grass.'

children.text: athālaṃkāraṇamalaṃkaraṇamasi sarvasmā alaṃ me bhūyāsam // ManGS_1,9.24 //
children.translated_text: Then the adornment: 'You are adornment; may I be sufficient for everything.'

children.text: praṇāpānau me tarpaya udīnarūpe me tarpaya sucakṣā aha makṣibhyāṃ bhūyāsaṃ suvarcā mukhena suśrutkarṇābhyāṃ bhūyāsāmiti yatāliṅgamaṅgāni saṃspṛśati // ManGS_1,9.25 //
children.translated_text: With 'Satisfy my <s>prāṇa</s> (inbreath) and <s>apāna</s> (outbreath); satisfy my risen form; may I be clear-sighted with my eyes, radiant with my face, well-hearing with my ears' — he touches the limbs according to their respective [mentions].
Then [comes] the anointing with fragrance and the garments.
'I shall clothe [myself], I shall bestow glory; for long life — may one reach old age;
may we live a hundred autumns, abundant; I shall provide for increase of progeny;
with glory may the earth, with glory <s>Indra</s> and <s>Bṛhaspati</s>,

children.text: yaśo bhagaśca māriṣadyaśo mā prati mucyatāmaṃ
children.translated_text: glory and <s>Bhaga</s> — may fortune be established [in me]; may glory be bestowed upon me.'
With this, he puts on an unworn garment.

children.text: kumāryāḥ pramadane bhagamaryamaṇaṃ pūṣaṇaṃ tvaṣṭāramiti yajati // ManGS_1,9.28 // /
children.translated_text: For the maiden's adornment, he makes offerings to <s>Bhaga</s>, <s>Aryaman</s>, <s>Pūṣan</s>, and <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>.
Before the <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s> (offering to Agni), four non-widowed [women] play the <s>nāndī</s> (auspicious music).
Within the <s>kautuka</s> (marriage enclosure), he makes offerings to the wives of the gods.
Thus ends the ninth section.
Tenth section.

children.text: prāgudañcaṃ lakṣaṇamuddhṛtyāvokṣya sthaṇiḍalaṃ gomayenopalipya maṇḍalaṃ caturasraṃ vā agniṃ nirmathyābhimukhaṃ praṇayet tatra brahmopaveśanam // ManGS_1,10.1 //
children.translated_text: Having drawn out the [sacred] mark extending eastward and northward, having sprinkled [it], having smeared the ground with cow-dung [to make] a circular or square [altar], having churned the fire, one should carry it forward facing [the altar]; there [is performed] the seating of <s>Brahmā</s> (the presiding priest).

children.text: darbhāṇāṃ pavitre mantravadutpādyemaṃstoma marhata ityagniṃ parisamuhya paryukṣya paristīrya paścādagnerekavadbahiḥstṛṇāti // ManGS_1,10.2 //
children.translated_text: Having produced the purificatory [instruments] of <s>darbha</s> grass with mantras, with 'Worship this <s>stoma</s> (hymn of praise),' having swept around the fire, having sprinkled around it, having strewn [grass] around it, to the west of the fire he strews [grass] outward in a single [layer].
Having drawn out <s>darbha</s> grasses with tips facing north and east, [he strews] the southern [ones] likewise and the northern ones past the fire, covering the northern [ones] with the southern.

children.text: dakṣiṇato 'gnerbrahmaṇe saṃstṛṇātyaparaṃ yajamānāya paścārjjhe patnyai aparamaparaṃśākhodakadhārayorlājā dhāryāśca paścādyugadhārasya ca // ManGS_1,10.4 //
children.translated_text: To the south of the fire, he strews [a seat] for <s>Brahmā</s> (the presiding priest); another for the sacrificer to the west; at the western side for the wife; yet another for the water-pot and ladle holders; the parched grains should be placed [there], and [a place] behind the yoke-holder.

children.text: syonā pṛthivi bhavetyetayāvasthāpya śamīmayīḥ śamyāḥ kṛtvāntagorṣṭhe 'gnimupasamādhāya bhartā bhāryāmabhyudānayati // ManGS_1,10.5 //
children.translated_text: Having established [the ground] with 'Be comfortable, O Earth,' having made pegs of <s>śamī</s> wood, having set up the fire at the edge of the cattle-pen, the husband leads the wife forward.
Having grasped the edge of her garment —

children.text: 'aghora cakṣurapatighnyedhi śivā paśubhyaḥ sumanāḥ suvarcāḥ vīrasūdervakāmā syonā śaṃ no bhava dvipade śaṃ catuṣpade' ityabhiparigṛhyābhyudānayati // ManGS_1,10.6 //
children.translated_text: 'O gentle one, be not fierce of eye, be not a husband-slayer, be auspicious to cattle, cheerful, radiant; be a bearer of heroes, fond of gods, gracious; be comfortable for us bipeds and quadrupeds' — embracing [her] around, he leads her forward.

children.text: uttareṇa rathaṃ vānovānuparikramyāntareṇa jvalanavahanāvatikramya dakṣiṇāsyāṃ dhuryuttarasya yugatanmano 'dhastātkanyāmavasthāpya śamyāmutkṛṣya hiraṇyamantardhāya hiraṇyavarṇāḥ śucaya iti tisṛbhiradbhirabhiṣicya ajtraiva bāṇaśabdaṃ kuruteti preṣyati // ManGS_1,10.7 //
children.translated_text: Having walked around to the north of the chariot or cart, having passed between [the fire and the vehicle] without crossing the flame and the conveyance, having stationed the maiden to the south of the pole-yoke of the northern draft-animal, below that mind[-directed point], having removed the peg, having placed gold in between, having sprinkled [her] with water with the three [verses] beginning 'Golden-hued, pure,' he commands: 'Make the sound of the arrow right here.'
Then he gives her the garment —
'Those [goddesses] who did not cut, who did not weave, who did not warp, who carried [the threads] —
and those divine women who stretched the ends all around —

children.text: tāstvādevyo jarase saṃvyayantvāyuṣmatīdaṃ paridhatsva vāsaḥ-ityahataṃ vāsaḥ- paridhāpyānvārabhyādhārāvājyabhāgau hutvā agnaye janavide svāhetyuttarārdhe juhoti somāya janavide svāheti dakṣiṇārddhe gandharvāya janavide svāheti madhye // ManGS_1,10.8 //
children.translated_text: may those goddesses clothe you for old age; O long-lived one, put on this garment' — having thus dressed [her] in an unworn garment, having had [her] hold on [to him], having offered the two <s>ādhāra</s> (base) oblations and the <s>ājyabhāga</s> (ghee-portion) oblations, he offers in the northern half 'To <s>Agni Janavid</s> (knower of people), <s>svāhā</s>,' in the southern half 'To <s>Soma Janavid</s>, <s>svāhā</s>,' and in the middle 'To <s>Gandharva Janavid</s>, <s>svāhā</s>.'

children.text: yukto vaha yadākūtamiti dvābhyāmagniṃyojayitvā nakṣatramiṣṭvā nakṣatradevatāṃyajettithiṃ tithidevatāmṛtudevatāṃ ca // ManGS_1,10.9 //
children.translated_text: Having yoked the fire with the two [verses] 'Yoked, carry what [our] intention [is],' having worshipped the <s>nakṣatra</s> (asterism), one should offer to the deity of the <s>nakṣatra</s>, to the <s>tithi</s> (lunar day), to the deity of the <s>tithi</s>, and to the deity of the <s>ṛtu</s> (season).
'<s>Soma</s> gave [her] to <s>Gandharva</s>, <s>Gandharva</s> gave [her] to <s>Agni</s>;
<s>Agni</s> gave me wealth and sons, and also this [bride].
<s>Agni</s> was her first [husband], <s>Jātavedas</s> (knower of all beings);
may he release her offspring from the bond of death.
May king <s>Varuṇa</s> approve of this,
that we have attained [her who brings] great-grandsons — to the <s>Rudriya</s> [deity], <s>svāhā</s>.'
With these, beginning with '<s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>' — eight [verses], he should offer <s>ājya</s> (ghee) oblations, one for each verse.

children.text: yena ca karmaṇecachettatra ca jayān juhuyāt jayānāṃca śrutistāṃ yatoktām /
children.translated_text: And for whatever rite one has undertaken, there also one should offer the <s>jaya</s> (victory) oblations; and the <s>śruti</s> (scriptural authority) for the <s>jaya</s> oblations is as stated [elsewhere].

children.text: ākūtyai tvā svāhā, bhūtyai tvā svāha, prayuje tevā svāha, nabhase tvā svāha, aryambhaṇe tvā svāha, samṛdhyai tvā svāha, jayāyai tvā svāha, kāmāya tvā svāhetyṛcā stomaṃ prajāpataya iti ca // ManGS_1,10.11 //
children.translated_text: 'To intention, <s>svāhā</s>; to prosperity, <s>svāhā</s>; to employment, <s>svāhā</s>; to the sky, <s>svāhā</s>; to nobility, <s>svāhā</s>; to success, <s>svāhā</s>; to victory, <s>svāhā</s>; to desire, <s>svāhā</s>' — with [these] verses and a <s>stoma</s> (hymn) to <s>Prajāpati</s>.
Pure, facing west, approaching [her], he says 'Look at me.'
As she looks [at him], he recites —

children.text: mama vrate te hṛdayaṃ dadhātu mama cittamanucittaṃ te 'stu
children.translated_text: 'May your heart be placed in my vow; may your mind follow my mind;

children.text: mama vācamekamanā juṣasva prajāpatiṣṭhvā niyunaktumahyam-iti // ManGS_1,10.13 //
children.translated_text: may you delight in my speech with single-mindedness; may <s>Prajāpati</s> join you to me.'
'What is your name?' — he asks.
When the name

children.text:
prokte devasya tvā savituḥ prasave 'śvinorbāhubhyāṃ pūṣṇo hastābhyāṃ hastaṃ gṛhṇābhyasāviti hastaṃ gṛhṇannāma gṛhṇāti /
prāṅmukhyāḥ prātyāṅmuka ūrdhvastiṣṭannāsīnāyā dakṣiṇa muttānaṃ dakṣiṇena nīcārikta mariktena- yathendrohastamagrahīt savitā varuṇo bhagaḥ /
children.translated_text: is declared: 'By the impulse of the god <s>Savitṛ</s>, with the arms of the two <s>Aśvins</s>, with the hands of <s>Pūṣan</s>, I grasp your hand, O so-and-so' — grasping [her] hand, he takes [her] name. [She stands] facing east, he facing west; he stands upright, she is seated; [he takes] the right [hand], palm upward, with the right [hand], palm downward — 'As <s>Indra</s> grasped the hand, as <s>Savitṛ</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Bhaga</s>,

children.text: gṛhṇāmi te sau bhagatvāya hastaṃ mayā patyā jaradṛṣṭiryathā sat //
children.translated_text: I grasp your hand, O so-and-so, for the sake of good fortune; with me as husband, may you reach old age.'

children.text: bhago aryamā savitā purandhir mahyaṃ tvādurgārhapatyāya dovāḥ /
children.translated_text: '<s>Bhaga</s>, <s>Aryaman</s>, <s>Savitṛ</s>, <s>Purandhī</s> — the gods [gave] you to me for the establishment of the household.'
'The speech that spoke first, before [the contest of] gods and demons —

children.text: tāmadya gāthāṃ gāsyāmo yā strīṇāmuttamaṃ manaḥ /
children.translated_text: that song we shall sing today, which is the highest thought of women.'
'O <s>Sarasvatī</s>, lead this one forward, O auspicious one, O <s>Vājinīvatī</s>;

children.text: yāṃ tvā viśvasya bhūtasya bhavyasya prāgāyāmyasyāgrataḥ /
children.translated_text: you whom I sing before all beings, past and future, at the forefront.'

children.text: amoha masmi sā tvaṃ sā tvamasyāpyamoham //
children.translated_text: 'I am he, you are she; you are she, I am he.

children.text: dyau rahaṃ pṛthivi tvamṛk tvamasi sāmāham //
children.translated_text: I am the sky, you are the earth; I am the <s>Ṛc</s> (Ṛg Veda), you are the <s>Sāman</s>.
I am the seed, you are the bearer of the seed.

children.text: tā eva vivāhāvahai puṃse putrāya karttavai /
children.translated_text: Let us two marry for the sake of a male child, for a son to be born,
for fortune and for a son, for progeny.'
'For wealth and progeny, for good offspring, for valor.'
Thus.
Having led [her] around clockwise, behind the fire —
'Step upon this stone; be firm as this stone.

children.text: kṛṇvantu viśve devā āyurvā śaradaḥ śatam /
children.translated_text: May all the gods grant [you] a life of a hundred autumns.'
With this, he makes [her] step on the stone with the right foot.
'As <s>Indra</s> descended with <s>Indrāṇī</s> from mount <s>Gandhamādana</s>,
so do you descend from this stone together with [your] wife.'

children.text: ārohasva same pādau pra pūrvyāyuṣmatī kanye putravatī bhava /
children.translated_text: 'Step upon the even [ground]; O maiden, long-lived, advance forward; be possessed of sons.'
Thus he makes [her] step [on the stone] twice.
He leads [her] around [the fire] four times.

children.text: samitaṃ saṃkalpethāmiti paryāye paryāye brahmā brahmajapaṃ japet // ManGS_1,10.19 //
children.translated_text: At each circumambulation, the <s>Brahmā</s> (presiding priest) should recite the <s>Brahmajapa</s> (sacred murmur) with 'May you be united in intention.'
Thus ends the tenth section.
Eleventh section.
Thereafter, the combination of rites should be understood according to [their] purpose.

children.text: aryamṇe 'gnaye pūṣṇe 'gnaye varuṇāya ca vrīhīn yavānvābhinirūpya prokṣya lājā bhṛjati // ManGS_1,11.2 //
children.translated_text: Having dedicated rice or barley grains to <s>Aryaman</s> and <s>Agni</s>, to <s>Pūṣan</s> and <s>Agni</s>, and to <s>Varuṇa</s>, having sprinkled [them], he parches the <s>lāja</s> (parched grains).

children.text: mātre prayacchati sa jātāyā avidhavāyai // ManGS_1,11.3 //
children.translated_text: He gives [them] to the mother who is a non-widow, born [of good family].

children.text: athāsyai dvitīyaṃ vāsaḥ prayacchati tenaiva mantreṇa // ManGS_1,11.4 //
children.translated_text: Then he gives her a second garment with the same mantra.

children.text: darbharajvā indraṇyāḥ saṃnahanamityantau samāyamya pumāṃsaṃ granthiṃ bandhnāti // ManGS_1,11.5 //
children.translated_text: With a rope of <s>darbha</s> grass, with [the verse] 'the girding of <s>Indrāṇī</s>,' having joined the two ends together, he ties a male knot.

children.text: saṃ tvā nahyāmi payasā pṛthivyāḥ saṃtvā nahyāmyadbhiroṣadhībhiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'I bind you with the milk of the earth; I bind you with waters and herbs;

children.text: saṃ tvā nahyāmi prajayā dhanena sā sannaddhā sunuhi bhāgadheyam /
children.translated_text: I bind you with offspring and wealth; thus bound, press out [your] share of fortune.'

children.text: itiyantarato vastrasya yoktreṇa kanyāṃ saṃnahyate // ManGS_1,11.6 //
children.translated_text: With this, from the inside of the garment, with a girdle, he binds the maiden.

children.text: athainānyupakalpayate śūrpāṃ lājā iṣīkā aśmāna māñjanam // ManGS_1,11.7 //
children.translated_text: Then he prepares these [items]: a winnowing basket, parched grains, a reed, a stone, and collyrium.

children.text: catasṛbhirdarbheṣīkābhiḥ śareṣīkābhirvā samuñajābhiḥ satūlābhirityekaikayā traikakubhasyāñjanasya saṃnikṛṣya vṛtrasyāsi kanīniketi bharturdakṣiṇamakṣi triḥ prathama māṅkte tathā paraṃ tathā patnyāḥ śeṣeṇa tūṣṇīm // ManGS_1,11.8 //
children.translated_text: With four blades of <s>darbha</s> grass or <s>śara</s> reed, bundled together and tufted, using each one, having drawn near the <s>añjana</s> (collyrium) of the three quarters, with the mantra 'You are the pupil of <s>Vṛtra</s>,' she anoints the right eye of the husband three times first, then the other, then the wife's; the remainder is applied silently. // ManGS_1,11.8 //

children.text: diśi śalākāḥ pravidhyati yāni rakṣāṃsyabhito vrajantyasyā vadhvā agnisakāśa māgacchantyāḥ teṣāmahaṃ pratividhyāmi cakṣuḥ svasti vadhvai
children.translated_text: She throws the sticks in the directions: 'Whatever <s>rakṣas</s> (demons) move about this bride as she approaches near the fire, I pierce their eyes. May there be well-being for the bride;
may <s>Bhūtapati</s> (Lord of beings) bestow it.'
Thus. // ManGS_1,11.9 //

children.text: lājāḥ paścādagnerupasādya śamīparṇaiḥ saṃyujya śūrpe samaṃ caturdhā vibhajyāgreṇāgniṃ paryāhṛtya lājādhāryai prayacchati // ManGS_1,11.10 //
children.translated_text: Having placed the parched grains behind the fire and mixed them with <s>śamī</s> leaves, dividing them equally into four portions in a winnowing basket, and having carried them around the fire to the front, he gives them to the one who holds the parched grains. // ManGS_1,11.10 //
A brother or a <s>brahmacārin</s> (celibate student) pours the parched grains from his joined hands into her joined hands. // ManGS_1,11.11 //
With the underlaying and pouring over of ghee, they offer those as an uninterrupted oblation into the confluence:
'The maiden has worshipped the god <s>Aryaman</s> through <s>Agni</s>;
may the god <s>Aryaman</s> release us from here, not from the husband. <s>Svāhā</s> (hail)!'
'For you, O <s>Agni</s>, they have brought <s>Sūryā</s> with the wedding procession.'

children.text: punaḥ patibhyo jāyāṃ dā agneḥ prajayā saha //
children.translated_text: 'Give the wife back to her husbands, O <s>Agni</s>, together with offspring.'
'Again <s>Agni</s> has given the wife with life and vigor;
long-lived be he who is her husband, may he live a hundred autumns.'
'This woman declares, while offering the parched grains into the fire:

children.text: dīrdhāyurastu me patiredhantāṃ jñātayo mameti // ManGS_1,11.12 //
children.translated_text: May my husband be long-lived, may my kinsmen prosper.' // ManGS_1,11.12 //

children.text: evaṃ pūṣaṇaṃ nu devaṃ varuṇaṃ nu devam // ManGS_1,11.13 //
children.translated_text: Likewise with 'the god <s>Pūṣan</s>' and 'the god <s>Varuṇa</s>.' // ManGS_1,11.13 //

children.text: yena dyau rugretyādaya udvāhe homā jayābyātānāḥ saṃtatihomā rāṣṭrabhṛtaśca // ManGS_1,11.14 //
children.translated_text: Beginning with 'By which the heaven,' the <s>jaya</s> (victory) oblations at the wedding, the <s>abhyātāna</s> (overpowering) oblations, the <s>saṃtati</s> (continuity) oblations, and the <s>rāṣṭrabhṛt</s> (kingdom-sustaining) oblations. // ManGS_1,11.14 //

children.text: ākūtāya svāheti jayāḥ prācī digvasanta ṛturityabhyātānāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'To intention, <s>svāhā</s>' — these are the <s>jaya</s> oblations; 'The eastern direction, spring the season' — these are the <s>abhyātāna</s> oblations;

children.text: prāṇādāpānaṃ saṃtanviti saṃtatihomā ṛtā ṣāḍṛtadhāmeti dvādaśarāṣṭrabhṛtaśca // ManGS_1,11.15 //
children.translated_text: 'From <s>prāṇa</s> (outbreath) to <s>apāna</s> (inbreath) he extends' — these are the <s>saṃtati</s> oblations; 'The seasons, the six seasons' abode' — these are the twelve <s>rāṣṭrabhṛt</s> oblations. // ManGS_1,11.15 //
'<s>Indra</s> the protector,' '<s>Viśvādityāḥ</s>' — these are for the benediction. // ManGS_1,11.16 //
The parched grains are offered optionally; not the fourth, nor the <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s> (oblation to the fire). // ManGS_1,11.17 //

children.text: athaināṃ prācīṃ saptapadāni prakramayatyekamiṣe dve ūrje trīṇi prajābhyaścatvāri rāyaspoṣāya pañca bhavāya ṣaḍṭatubhyaḥ--
children.translated_text: Then he makes her take seven steps forward toward the east: 'One for food, two for vitality, three for offspring, four for increase of wealth, five for prosperity, six for the seasons —
be a friend with the seventh, O gracious <s>Sarasvatī</s>;
may your appearance not be lost from sight.'
'May <s>Viṣṇu</s> lead you forth' — this he appends everywhere. // ManGS_1,11.18 //

children.text: paścādagre rohite carmaṇyānajuḍuhe prāggrīve lomato darbhānāstīrya teṣu vadhūmupaveśayatyapi vā darbheṣveva // ManGS_1,11.19 //
children.translated_text: Behind the fire, on a red bull-hide with the neck facing east, having spread <s>darbha</s> grass with the hair side up, he seats the bride on them; or alternatively, on <s>darbha</s> grass alone. // ManGS_1,14.7 // // ManGS_1,11.19 //

children.text: imaṃviṣyāmi varuṇasya pāśaṃ yajjagrantha savitā satyadharmā /
children.translated_text: 'I loosen this snare of <s>Varuṇa</s>, which <s>Savitṛ</s> of true law has bound;

children.text: dhātuśca yonau sukṛtasya loke riṣṭāṃ mā saha patyā dadhātu //
children.translated_text: may <s>Dhātṛ</s> place me unharmed together with my husband in the womb of well-doing, in the world of merit.'

children.text: iti yokrapāśaṃ viṣāya vāsaso 'nte badhnāti // ManGS_1,11.20 //
children.translated_text: Thus, having loosened the yoke-rope snare, he ties it at the edge of the garment. // ManGS_1,11.20 //

children.text: anumatibhyāṃ vyāhṛtibhyaśca tvanno agne , ayāścāgnesīti ca // ManGS_1,11.21 //
children.translated_text: With the two <s>Anumati</s> verses, with the <s>Vyāhṛtis</s> (sacred utterances), and with 'You, O <s>Agni</s>, for us' and 'O <s>Agni</s>, you are.' // ManGS_1,11.21 //

Three anointed <s>samidhs</s> (fuel sticks) of <s>śamī</s> wood — with the three verses beginning 'From the ocean with waves,' ending with <s>svāhā</s>, he places them on the fire. // ManGS_1,11.22 //

children.text: akṣata saktūnāṃ dadhnaśca samavadāyedaṃ haviḥ prajananaṃ ma iti hutyājyenābhijuhoti // ManGS_1,11.23 //
children.translated_text: Having mixed together unhusked rice, barley flour, and curds, with the mantra 'This oblation is generative for me,' after offering it, he makes an additional offering with ghee. // ManGS_1,11.23 //
They purify themselves with water from a pitcher, with the <s>Āpohiṣṭhīya</s> verses. // ManGS_1,11.26 //
A bull is the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (sacrificial fee). // ManGS_1,11.27 //
Thus ends the eleventh section. //11//
Twelfth section.
'Auspicious is this bride; come together and behold her;
having given her good fortune, then depart.'
With this he bids farewell to the onlookers as they leave. // ManGS_1,12.1 //

children.text: atraiva sīmantaṃ karoti trīśyetayā śalalyā samūlena vā darbheṇa senāhanāmetyetayā // ManGS_1,12.2 //
children.translated_text: Right there he parts her hair with a porcupine quill or with a <s>darbha</s> grass blade including the root, with the mantra 'Of the army.' // ManGS_1,12.2 //
Then they anoint her:
'Anointing the hair, being of good mind, rich in offspring, famous, having many sons, not fierce,
auspicious for the husband, having come to the father-in-law's home, long-lived, possessing a mother-in-law, of long life.'
Thus. // ManGS_1,12.3 //
She binds up with living wool:

children.text: samasya keśānavṛjinānaghorān śikhā sakhībhyo bhava sarvābhyaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Arrange the hair, not crooked, not fierce; be a topknot-friend to all;
be auspicious, being of good family; be auspicious among people, among those who travel together.'
Thus. // ManGS_1,12.4 //

children.text: athaino dadhimadhu samaśruto yadvā haviṣyaṃ syāt // ManGS_1,12.5 //
children.translated_text: Then they offer her curds and honey mixed together, or whatever would be suitable as an offering. // ManGS_1,12.5 //

children.text: tasya svasti vācayitvā samānā vā ākūtānīti saha japanti // ManGS_1,12.6 //
children.translated_text: Having pronounced a blessing over it, they recite together 'May our intentions be the same.' // ManGS_1,12.6 //
Both eat together. // ManGS_1,12.7 //
Thus ends the twelfth section. //12//
Thirteenth section.
On an auspicious day he yokes the cart. // ManGS_1,13.1 //

children.text: yuñjanti bradhnamiti dvābhyāṃ yujyamānamanumantrayate dakṣiṇamathottaram // ManGS_1,13.2 //
children.translated_text: With the two verses beginning 'They yoke the tawny one,' he addresses the one being yoked — the right one first, then the left. // ManGS_1,13.2 //

children.text: ahatena vāsasā darbhairvā rathaṃ saṃmārṣṭi // ManGS_1,13.3 //
children.translated_text: He wipes the chariot with a new garment or with <s>darbha</s> grass. // ManGS_1,13.3 //

children.text: ahkūnyaṅkāvabito rathaṃ ye dhāvantā vātā agnimabhiye saṃcaranti dūre hetiḥ patatrī vājinī vāṃste no 'gnayaḥ paprayaḥ pālayantu iti cakre abhimantrayate // ManGS_1,13.4 //
children.translated_text: With 'The curved hooks that run about the chariot, the winds that rush together toward <s>Agni</s> — far be the winged, swift weapon; may those fires protect us as we go forth,' he addresses the wheels. // ManGS_1,13.4 //
'O lord of the forest, with firm limbs' — this is for the standing-place (platform of the chariot). // ManGS_1,13.5 //

children.text: sukiṃ śukraṃ śalmaliṃ viśvarūpaṃ hiraṇyavarṇaṃ suvṛtaṃ sucakram āroha sūrye amṛtasya lokaṃ syonaṃ patye vahataṃ, kṛṇuṣva //
children.translated_text: 'The auspicious, bright, <s>śalmalī</s>-like, of all forms, golden-hued, well-turned, fair-wheeled — mount, O <s>Sūrya</s>, the world of immortality; make the conveyance pleasant for the husband.'
With this he makes her mount. // ManGS_1,13.6 //
'May the gods follow along, may <s>Brahman</s> follow with good heroism;
may royal power and strength follow along, may glory follow me.'
With this, having driven forward to the east, he turns to the right (clockwise). // ManGS_1,13.7 //
'May the gods come to meet us, may <s>Brahman</s> come with good heroism;

children.text: pratikṣatraṃ tu yadbalaṃ prati māmaitu yadyaśaḥ //
children.translated_text: may royal power and strength come to meet us, may glory come to meet me.'
With this he addresses them as they go toward their home. // ManGS_1,13.8 //
If they pass by something inauspicious, he recites 'May they follow along.' // ManGS_1,13.9 //

children.text: namo rudrāya grāmasada iti grāme imā rudrāyeti ca // ManGS_1,13.10 //
children.translated_text: 'Homage to <s>Rudra</s> who dwells in the village' — in a village; and 'These to <s>Rudra</s>.' // ManGS_1,13.10 //
'Homage to <s>Rudra</s> who dwells by a single tree' — at a solitary tree;
and 'Those who are in the trees, reddish-yellow.' // ManGS_1,13.11 //
'Homage to <s>Rudra</s> who dwells in the cremation ground' — at a cremation ground;
and 'Those who are lords of beings.' // ManGS_1,13.12 //
'Homage to <s>Rudra</s> who dwells at the crossroads' — at a crossroads;

children.text: 'ye pathāṃ pathi rakṣaya' iti ca // ManGS_1,13.13 //
children.translated_text: and 'Those who guard the paths on the road.' // ManGS_1,13.13 //
'Homage to <s>Rudra</s> who dwells at the ford' — at a ford;
and 'Those who roam the fords.' // ManGS_1,13.14 //

children.text: yatrāpastaritavyā āsīditi samudrāya vaiṇave sindhūnāṃ pataye namaḥ /

children.translated_text: homage to the lord of all rivers;

children.text: viśvāhā juṣatāṃ viśvakarmaṇāmidaṃ haviḥ svaḥ svāhetyapsūdakāñjalīnninayati /
children.translated_text: may <s>Viśvakarman</s> always enjoy this oblation — <s>svaḥ</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!' He lowers handfuls of water into the water.

children.text: amṛtaṃ vā āsye juhomyāyuḥ prāṇe 'pyamṛtaṃ brahmaṇā saha mṛtyuntarati /
children.translated_text: 'I offer <s>amṛta</s> (nectar) into the mouth; immortality together with <s>Brahman</s> into the <s>prāṇa</s> (life-breath) — one crosses death.'

children.text: prāsahāditi riṣṭiriti muktiriti mukṣīyamāṇaḥ sarvaṃ bhayaṃ nudasva svāheti triḥ parimṛjyācāmati // ManGS_1,13.15 //
children.translated_text: 'From overpowering — safety; from that — release; being released, drive away all fear — <s>svāhā</s>!' Having sipped water three times, he performs <s>ācamana</s> (ritual sipping). // ManGS_1,13.15 //
Where water must be crossed: 'Homage to the ocean, to the bamboo-lord, to the lord of rivers;

children.text: yadi nāvā taret sutrāmāṇamiti japet // ManGS_1,13.16 //
children.translated_text: If one crosses by a boat, one should recite the <s>Sutrāmāṇa</s> hymn. // ManGS_1,13.16 //

children.text: yadi rathākṣaḥ śamyāṇīvā riṣyetānyadvā rathāṅgaṃ tatraivāgnibhupasamādhāya jayaprabhṛtibhirhutvā sumaṅgalīriyaṃ vadhūriti japet vadhvā saha vadhūṃ sameta paśyata // ManGS_1,13.17 //
children.translated_text: If the chariot axle or the pin breaks, or any other part of the chariot, right there having set up a fire, having offered with the <s>jaya</s> oblations and the rest, he should recite 'Auspicious is this bride,' and 'Come together and behold the bride' together with the bride. // ManGS_1,13.17 //

children.text: vyutkrāma panthāṃ jaritāṃ javena śivena vaiśvānara iḍyāsyāgrataḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Step aside from the path swiftly, O singer; auspicious <s>Vaiśvānara</s> (Fire), worthy of worship, be in front;

children.text: ācāryo yena yena pathā prayāti tena tena saha //
children.translated_text: by whatever path the teacher goes, by that path together.'
With this, both step aside. // ManGS_1,13.18 //

children.text: gobhiḥ sahāstāmite grāmaṃ praviśanti brāhmaṇavacanādvā // ManGS_1,13.19 //
children.translated_text: They enter the village together with cows at sunset, or at the word of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. // ManGS_1,13.19 //
Thus ends the thirteenth section. //13//
Fourteenth section.
On the following day, at twilight, he should bring her to the house. // ManGS_1,14.1 //
With 'Counter, O <s>Brahman</s>,' she descends. // ManGS_1,14.2 //
Auspicious signs appear. // ManGS_1,14.3 //
From the cow-pen he spreads an unbroken line of <s>ulapa</s> grass. // ManGS_1,14.4 //
From the chariot up to the place of the sacred fire:
'Those homes in which one who is away dwells, in which there is great joy of mind,
with those we invite you; may they recognize your arrival.'
With this she approaches. // ManGS_1,14.5 //

children.text: gṛhānahṃ sumanasaḥ prapadye vīraṃ hi vīravataḥ suśevā
children.translated_text: 'I approach the houses with a glad mind, for they are gracious, providing heroes to the heroic;
bearing nourishment, dripping with ghee — in those may I dwell with a glad mind.'

children.text: ityabhyāhitīgniṃsohakaṃ sauṣadhamāvasathaṃ pratipadyate rohiṇyā mūlena vā yadvā puṇyoktam // ManGS_1,14.6 //
children.translated_text: With this she enters the dwelling where the fire has been brought, the <s>sauṣadha</s> (healing) abode, on the <s>Rohiṇī</s> constellation or at whatever time is declared auspicious. // ManGS_1,14.6 //

children.text: paścādagne rohite carmaṇyānaḍuhe prāggrīve lomato darbhānastīrya teṣu vadhūmupaveśayatyapi vā darbheṣveva // ManGS_1,14.7 //
children.translated_text: Behind the fire, on a red bull-hide with the neck facing east, having spread <s>darbha</s> grass with the hair side up, he seats the bride on them; or alternatively, on <s>darbha</s> grass alone. // ManGS_1,14.7 //
Then he places a celibate boy in her lap:
'Through <s>Soma</s> the <s>Ādityas</s> are strong, through <s>Soma</s> the earth is great;
and <s>Soma</s> is placed in the lap of these stars.'
Thus. // ManGS_1,14.8 //

children.text: athāsya tilataṇḍulānāṃ phalamiśrāṇāmañjaliṃ pūrayitvotthāpyāthāsyai dhrumaruṅatīṃ jīvattīṃ saptaṛṣīniti darśayet // ManGS_1,14.9 //
children.translated_text: Then, having filled her joined hands with sesame seeds, rice grains mixed with fruits, and having raised her up, he shows her <s>Dhruva</s> (the Pole Star), <s>Arundhatī</s>, the living one, and the Seven Sages. // ManGS_1,14.9 //

children.text: acyutā dhruvā dhruvapatnī druvaṃ paśyema sarvataḥ
children.translated_text: 'Unfallen, firm — as the firm wife of the firm one, may we see from all sides;

children.text: dhruvāsaḥ parvatā ime dhruvā strī patikuleyam //
children.translated_text: firm are these mountains, firm is this woman in her husband's family.'
Thus he recites while she gazes upon it. // ManGS_1,14.10 //

children.text: śvabhūte prājāpatyaṃ payasi sthālīpākaṃ śrapayitvā tasya juhoti /
children.translated_text: On the following day, he cooks a <s>sthālīpāka</s> (rice porridge) sacred to <s>Prajāpati</s> in milk and offers from it;
in the remainder of the ghee, having brought curds, he offers with the remnant of the oblation. // ManGS_1,14.11 //

children.text: cakrīvānaḍuhau vā me vāṅmaitu te manaḥ
children.translated_text: 'As the <s>cakravāka</s> bird and the bull — may my speech go to you, may your mind come to me;

children.text: cākravākaṃ saṃ vananaṃ tannau saṃ vananaṃ kṛtam-
children.translated_text: the <s>cakravāka</s>-like union — that union has been made for us.'

children.text: iti yajamānastriḥ prāśnātyavaśiṣṭaṃ tūṣṇīṃ patnī // ManGS_1,14.12 //
children.translated_text: With this the sacrificer eats three times; the wife silently eats the remainder. // ManGS_1,14.12 //
In the afternoon the <s>Piṇḍapitṛyajña</s> (offering of rice balls to the ancestors) is performed; it has been explained. // ManGS_1,14.13 //

children.text: saṃvatsaraṃ brahmacaryaṃ carato dvādaśarātraṃ trirātramekakarātraṃ vā // ManGS_1,14.14 //
children.translated_text: They observe <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibacy) for a year, or for twelve nights, or three nights, or one night. // ManGS_1,14.14 //
Then he should let her go to her own house. // ManGS_1,14.15 //
Having loosened the yoke-rope, he should bring the two together:

children.text: apaśyaṃ tvā manasā dīdhyānāṃ svāyāṃ tanuṃṛtviye bādhamānām /
children.translated_text: 'I beheld you meditating in mind, pressing yourself in your own body for the season of conception;

children.text: upa māmuccā yuvatirbabhūyāḥ prajāyasva prajāyasva prajayā putrakāme //
children.translated_text: come up to me, O young woman — may you bear offspring, bear offspring, O desirous of a son, with offspring.'

children.text: prajāpatistanvaṃ me juṣasva tvaṣṭā devaiḥ sahamāna indraḥ /
children.translated_text: 'May <s>Prajāpati</s> delight in my body; <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> with the gods, <s>Indra</s> the mighty;

children.text: viśvedevairṛtubhiḥ saṃ vidānaḥ puṃsāṃ bahūnāṃ mātarau syāva //
children.translated_text: knowing together with all the gods and the seasons, may we two become the parents of many sons.'
'I place the embryo in the herbs, I in all the worlds within;

children.text: ahaṃ prajā ajanayaṃ pṛthivyā haṃ janibhyo aparīṣu putrān //
children.translated_text: I have generated offspring on the earth, I have given sons to women in later births.'
Thus he recites with the interchange of the feminine and other forms. // ManGS_1,14.16 //
With '<s>kara</s>' (do!) he touches her with the <s>bhasma</s> (ashes). // ManGS_1,14.17 //
With '<s>jananī</s>' (mother) — the approach for generation. // ManGS_1,14.18 //
With '<s>bṛhat</s>' (great) — the child born is established. // ManGS_1,14.19 //
By this rule, he should unite with her at each season of conception. // ManGS_1,14.20 //
Thus ends the fourteenth section. //14//
Fifteenth section.

children.text: tṛtīye garbhamāse araṇī āhṛtya ṣaṣṭhe 'ṣṭhame vā jayaprabhṛtibhirhutvā paścādagnerdarbheṣvāsīnīyāḥ patnyāḥ sarvān pramucya keśānnavanītenābhyajya--
triśyenayā śalalyā śamīśākhayā ca sa palāśayā punaḥ patnīmagniradāditi sīmantaṃ karoti // ManGS_1,15.1 //
children.translated_text: with a porcupine quill, a <s>śamī</s> branch together with <s>palāśa</s> leaves, and with the verse 'Again <s>Agni</s> has given the wife,' he performs the <s>sīmantonnayana</s> (parting of the hair ceremony). // ManGS_1,15.1 //

In the third month of pregnancy, having brought the fire-sticks, or in the sixth or eighth month, having offered with the <s>jaya</s> oblations and the rest, behind the fire, the wife being seated on <s>darbha</s> grass, having loosened all her hair, having anointed it with fresh butter —
Thus ends the fifteenth section. //15//
Sixteenth section.

children.text: aṣṭhame garbhamāse jayaprabhṛtibhirhurvā phalaiḥ snāpasitvā yā oṣadhaya ityanuvākenāhatena vāsasā pracchādya gandhapuṣpairalaṃkṛtya phalāni kaṇṭhe vai saṃsṛjyāgniṃ pradakṣiṇaṃ kuryāt // ManGS_1,16.1 //
children.translated_text: In the eighth month of pregnancy, having offered with the <s>jaya</s> oblations and the rest, having bathed her with fruits, with the <s>anuvāka</s> 'Which herbs,' having covered her with a new garment, having adorned her with scents and flowers, having placed fruits around her neck, she should go around the fire keeping it to the right. // ManGS_1,16.1 //

children.text: prajāṃ me naryapāhīti mantreṇopasthānaṃ kṛtvā guṇavato brāhmaṇān bhojayet // ManGS_1,16.2 //
children.translated_text: Having performed the invocation with the mantra 'Protect my offspring, O man,' he should feed virtuous <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>. // ManGS_1,16.2 //
He should give fruits as the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (sacrificial fee). // ManGS_1,16.3 //
Then the <s>svastyayana</s> (benedictory ceremony) also. // ManGS_1,16.4 //
Whoever is the elder, him he should honor. // ManGS_1,16.5 //
Thus ends the sixteenth section. //16//
Seventeenth section.
When a son is born, he gives a gift. // ManGS_1,17.1 //
Having churned fire from the fire-sticks, he should offer the <s>āyuṣya</s> (longevity) oblations in that fire. // ManGS_1,17.2 //
With the <s>anuvāka</s> beginning '<s>Agni</s> is life,' he offers twenty-one ghee oblations, verse by verse, section by section. // ManGS_1,17.3 //

children.text: ājyaśeṣe dadhimadhvapo hiraṇyaśakalenopahatya triḥ prāśāpayati // ManGS_1,17.4 //
children.translated_text: In the remainder of the ghee, having mixed curds, honey, and water with a gold chip, he makes the child eat three times. // ManGS_1,17.4 //
'Be a stone, be an axe, be gold uncut;

children.text: vedo vai putranāmāsi sajīva śaradaḥ śatam //
children.translated_text: you are the <s>Veda</s> by name, O son — live a hundred autumns.'

children.text: iti prādeśenādhyadhi pratimukhaṃ pradakṣiṇaṃ sarvato 'bhyuddhiśati // ManGS_1,17.5 //
children.translated_text: With this, measuring with a span, he consecrates the child by touching face to face, clockwise, from all sides. // ManGS_1,17.5 //

children.text: bhūste dadāmīti dakṣiṇe bhuvastedadāmīti savye svaste dadāmīti dakṣiṇe bhūrbhuvaḥ- svaste dadāmīti savye // ManGS_1,17.6 //
children.translated_text: "<s>Bhūḥ</s>, I give to you" on the right [breast], "<s>Bhuvaḥ</s>, I give to you" on the left, "<s>Svaḥ</s>, I give to you" on the right, "<s>Bhūr-bhuvaḥ-svaḥ</s>, I give to you" on the left. // ManGS 1.17.6 //
Having inserted the middle leaf of a <s>palāśa</s> tree, with that he recites into the child's ears —

children.text: iṣaṃ pinvorjaṃ pinveti stanau pradhāpayet // ManGS_1,17.7 //
children.translated_text: He should make [the child] suckle the breasts [reciting] "<s>iṣaṃ pinva</s>, <s>ūrjaṃ pinva</s>" ("Flow with nourishment, flow with vigor"). // ManGS 1.17.7 //
Thus ends the seventeenth section. //17//
Eighteenth section.

children.text: daśamyāṃ rātryāṃ putrasya nāma dadhyād ghoṣavadādyantarantasthaṃ dvayakṣaraṃ caturakṣaraṃvā tryakṣaraṃ dāntaṃ kumārīṇām // ManGS_1,18.1 //
children.translated_text: On the tenth night, one should give the son a name that has a sonorous letter at the beginning or end or middle, with a semivowel, of two syllables or four syllables; for girls, of three syllables ending in a dental. // ManGS 1.18.1 //

children.text: tenābhivādayituṃ tyatkā piturnāmadheyaṃ yaśasyaṃ nāmadheyaṃ devatāśrayaṃ nakṣatrāśrayaṃ devatāyāśca pratyakṣam pratiṣiddham // ManGS_1,18.2 //
children.translated_text: By that [name] he should be made to offer salutation; it should avoid the father's name; it should be a glorious name, connected with a deity, connected with a <s>nakṣatra</s> (lunar mansion), and directly [indicating] the deity, [but] not a prohibited [name]. // ManGS 1.18.2 //
Having bathed, [the father] together with the son approaches [the fire]. // ManGS 1.18.3 //

children.text: athainamabhibhṛśati-'agneṣṭvā tejasā sūryasya varcasā viśveṣāṃ tvā devānāṃ kratunābhibhṛśāmīti prakṣālitapāṇirnavanītenābhyājyāgnau pratāpya brāhmaṇāya procyabhibhṛsediti śrutiḥ // ManGS_1,18.4 //
children.translated_text: Then he touches him [saying]: "With the splendor of <s>Agni</s>, with the radiance of <s>Sūrya</s>, with the wisdom of all the <s>Devas</s>, I touch you." Having washed his hands, anointing [the child] with fresh butter, warming [it] in the fire, and announcing to a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, he should touch [the child]—thus is the <s>śruti</s> (revealed text). // ManGS 1.18.4 //
He gives a gift to the performer [of the ceremony]. // ManGS 1.18.5 //

children.text:
aṅgādaṅgātsaṃbhavasi hṛdayādadhijāyase
ātmā vai putranāmāsi sa jīva śaradaḥ śatam //
children.translated_text:
"From limb to limb you are born, from the heart you are produced;
you are indeed the self named 'son'—may you live a hundred autumns."

children.text: iti pravāsādetya putrasya mūrddhani japet // ManGS_1,18.6 //
children.translated_text: Thus, upon returning from a journey, he should recite [this] over the son's head. // ManGS 1.18.6 //
He should not eat honey or meat until the <s>paśubandha</s> (animal sacrifice). // ManGS 1.18.7 //
And in [the first] year, he should sacrifice to <s>Agni</s> and <s>Dhanvantari</s> with [the milk of] goats and sheep. // ManGS 1.18.8 //
Thus ends the eighteenth section. //18//
Nineteenth section.
Now, the showing [of the child] to the sun. // ManGS 1.19.1 //

children.text: caturthe māsi payasi stālīpākaṃ śrapayitvā tasya juhoti // ManGS_1,19.2 //
children.translated_text: In the fourth month, having cooked a <s>sthālīpāka</s> (oblation cooked in a pot) in milk, he makes offerings from it. // ManGS 1.19.2 //
<s>Ādityaḥ śukraḥ</s> ("The Sun, the bright one")—

children.text: udagātpurastāddhaṃ saḥ śuciṣad yadedenamiti sūryasya juhoti // ManGS_1,19.3 //
children.translated_text: "He rose up from the east, he the pure one, that which is this"—with this [verse] he offers to <s>Sūrya</s>. // ManGS 1.19.3 //
Having worshipped with "<s>ud u tyaṃ jātavedasam</s>" ("Rise up, O <s>Jātavedas</s>"), he should show [the child] facing the sun—
"Salutation to you, O blessed one, O hundred-rayed one, O dispeller of darkness!

children.text: jahi me devadaurbhāgyaṃ saubhāgyena māṃ saṃyojayasva' /
children.translated_text: Destroy my ill-fortune and unite me with good fortune."
Thus. // ManGS 1.19.4 //
Then, the feeding of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>. // ManGS 1.19.5 //
A bull is the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (sacrificial fee). // ManGS 1.19.6 //
Thus ends the nineteenth section. //19//
Twentieth section.
Now, the first feeding [of solid food]. // ManGS 1.20.1 //

children.text: pañcame ṣaṣṭhe vā māsi payasi sthālīpākaṃ śrapayitvā snātamalaṅkṛtamahatena vāsasā pracchādyānnapate 'nnasya no dehīti hutvā hiraṇyena prāśayedannātparisruta ityṛcā // ManGS_1,20.2 //
children.translated_text: In the fifth or sixth month, having cooked a <s>sthālīpāka</s> (oblation cooked in a pot) in milk, having bathed and adorned [the child], covering [him] with a new garment, having offered with "O Lord of food, give us food," he should feed [the child] with gold [spoon, reciting] the <s>ṛc</s> (verse) "<s>annātparisrutaḥ</s>." // ManGS 1.20.2 //
He should show [the child] jewels, gold ornaments, and weapons. // ManGS 1.20.3 //
Whichever [the child] desires, that he should grasp. // ManGS 1.20.4 //
Then the feeding of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>. // ManGS 1.20.5 //
A garment is the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (sacrificial fee). // ManGS 1.20.6 //
Thus ends the twentieth section. //20//
Twenty-first section.

children.text: tṛtīyasya varṣasya bhūyiṣṭe gate cūḍāḥ kārayet //
children.translated_text: When the greater part of the third year has passed, he should have the <s>cūḍā</s> (tonsure) performed.

children.text: udagayane jyautsne puṇye nakṣatre 'nyatra navābhyām // ManGS_1,21.1 //
children.translated_text: During the northern course [of the sun], in the bright fortnight, under an auspicious <s>nakṣatra</s> (lunar mansion), except the ninth [day]. // ManGS 1.21.1 //
Having offered the <s>jaya</s> [oblations] and the following—
"With hot [water], <s>Vāyu</s> [purifies] with water; with the life-span of the sacrificer, <s>Savitṛ</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s> bestow upon the sacrificer, the generous one."
With this [mantra] he consecrates the hot water. // ManGS 1.21.2 //

children.text:
aditiḥ keśānvapatvāya udantu jīvase
dhārayatu prajāpatiḥ punaḥ punaḥ svastaye' //
children.translated_text:
"May <s>Aditi</s> shave the hair; may they rise up for life;
may <s>Prajāpati</s> sustain, again and again, for well-being."
With this [mantra] he sprinkles [the water] upward. // ManGS 1.21.3 //
"O herb, protect him"—with this [mantra] he places a <s>darbha</s> (sacred grass) blade at the right tuft of hair. // ManGS 1.21.4 //
"O razor, do not harm him"—with this [mantra] he applies the razor. // ManGS 1.21.5 //

children.text: yenāvapatsavitā kṣureṇa somasya rājño varuṇasya keśān /
children.translated_text: "With which razor <s>Savitṛ</s> shaved the hair of King <s>Soma</s> and of <s>Varuṇa</s>,
with that let the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> shave—may this one be long-lived, reaching old age firmly."
"With which [razor] <s>Pūṣan</s> shaved [the hair] of <s>Bṛhaspati</s> for vitality and long life,
with that we shave you for long life, for longevity, for living."
"By which one moves about more and sees the sun for long,
with that we shave you for long life, for good renown, for well-being."
With these three [verses] he shaves three times. // ManGS 1.21.6 //
"When with the razor of sharp edge, O barber, you shave the hair,
purify the head, do not cut short [his] life-span."

children.text: iti lauhāyasaṃ kṣuraṃ keśāvāpāya prayacchati // ManGS_1,21.7 //
children.translated_text: With this [mantra] he gives the iron razor to the barber for the hair-shaving. // ManGS 1.21.7 //

children.text: mā te keśānanugādvarca etattathā dhātā dadhātu te /
children.translated_text: "Let not your hair be destroyed nor your splendor; thus may <s>Dhātṛ</s> bestow upon you;

children.text: tubhyamindro varuṇo bṛhaspatiḥ savitā varcā ādadhuḥ //
children.translated_text: for you, <s>Indra</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, and <s>Savitṛ</s> have bestowed splendor."
With this [mantra] he blesses [the child] while [the barber] is shaving. // ManGS 1.21.8 //
He gathers [the hair] with the accompaniment of friends, in a lump of fresh cow-dung. // ManGS 1.21.9 //

children.text: uptvāya keśānvaruṇāsya rājño bṛhaspatiḥ savitā viṣṇuragniḥ /
children.translated_text: "Having shaved the hair, <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, <s>Savitṛ</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Agni</s>, [acting] for King <s>Varuṇa</s>,

children.text: tebhyo nidhānaṃ mahataṃ na vidannantarā dyāvāpṛthivyorapasyuḥ //
children.translated_text: not knowing a great repository for them, concealed them between heaven and earth."
