With this [mantra] he blesses [the hair] as it is being carried toward the northeast. // ManGS 1.21.10 //

children.translated_text: But for one who desires intelligence, having smeared a <s>palāśa</s> (Butea frondosa) [leaf] with fresh butter, he should teach in its shade:
O <s>Suśravas</s> (one of good fame), you are of good fame;

children.text: yathā tvaṃsuśravaḥ suśravā asi evaṃ māṃ suśravaḥ sauśravasaṃ kuru //
children.translated_text: just as you, O <s>Suśravas</s>, are of good fame, so make me of good fame, a descendant of <s>Suśravas</s>.

children.text: yathā tvaṃ devānāṃ vedānāṃ nidhipo asi /
children.translated_text: Just as you are the guardian of the <s>Vedas</s> among the gods,
so may I become the guardian of the <s>Vedas</s> among men. //17//

children.text: (adhīteha vā ayameṣāṃ vedānāmekaṃ dvau trīn sarvānveti yamenaṃ vidvāṃsamupanayatīti śrutiḥ //18//
children.translated_text: (Whether he has studied one, two, three, or all of these <s>Vedas</s>—this is the <s>śruti</s> (sacred tradition): he goes [to the same reward] as the learned one who initiates him. //18//
The <s>brahmacarya</s> (studentship) has been explained. //19//

children.text: atha bhaikṣaṃ carate mātaramevāgre yāścānyāḥ suhṛdo yāvatyo vā sannihitāḥ syuḥ //20//
children.translated_text: Then he goes for alms—first to his mother, and to whatever other well-wishers are present. //20//

children.text: ācāryāya bhaikṣamupakalpayate tenānujñāto vā bhuñjīteti śrutiḥ //21//
children.translated_text: He prepares the alms food for the <s>ācārya</s> (teacher); or, permitted by him, he may eat—this is the <s>śruti</s> (sacred tradition). //21//
Second <s>puruṣa</s> (book).
One whose father has died should establish the <s>śālāgni</s> (household fire) using the wedding fire. // ManGS_2,1.1 //

children.text: anyatra tataḥ prete pitari prajvalanto 'gniṃ jāgarayeyuḥ parvaṇi jyaitsne puṇye nakṣatre 'nyatra navamyāḥ // ManGS_2,1.2 //
children.translated_text: Otherwise, when the father has died, they should keep the fire blazing on the <s>parvan</s> (sacred day), on a bright [fortnight], under an auspicious <s>nakṣatra</s> (constellation), except on the ninth [day]. // ManGS_2,1.2 //
Having bathed, pure, wearing new garments. // ManGS_2,1.3 //
Observing silence, with fire-kindling sticks, keeping awake. // ManGS_2,1.4 //
In an open space, having ground unhusked grains and other [ingredients], he churns the <s>mantha</s> (ritual drink) abundantly with a sugarcane stick, without support. // ManGS_2,1.5 //
We invoke <s>Savitṛ</s> of golden hands, <s>Vāyu</s>, <s>Indra</s>, <s>Prajāpati</s>,
all the <s>Devas</s> (gods) and the <s>Aṅgirases</s>;
may they pacify that flesh-eating fire.
With this <s>mantha</s> (ritual drink) he extinguishes the fire. // ManGS_2,1.6 //
May king <s>Soma</s> distribute, and <s>Agni</s> distributing;
may the <s>havyavāhana</s> (oblation-carrying) fire remain here; push away the flesh-eating [fire].

children.text: iti kaṭe kṛtāyāṃ vāgniṃsamāropya prahiṇoti // ManGS_2,1.7 //
children.translated_text: Thus, having placed the fire on a mat, he sends it away. // ManGS_2,1.7 //

children.text: kravyādamagniṃ prahiṇomi dūraṃ yamarājyaṃ gacchatu ripravāhaḥ /
children.translated_text: I send far away the flesh-eating fire; may it go to the realm of <s>Yama</s>, the carrier of impurity.

children.text: ihaivāyamitaro jātavedā devebhyo havyā vahatu prajānan //
children.translated_text: May this other <s>Jātavedas</s> (fire) remain here, carrying oblations to the gods with knowledge.
Thus, taking the fire, they carry it south and west. // ManGS_2,1.8 //
They go along with the implements. // ManGS_2,1.9 //
In a self-made barren place—
In the lead [vessel] we deposit the evil spirits, with the head as a pillow,
upon the unwoven black [cloth], the destroyers of the dead have been removed.
Thus he places the lead as a pillow upon the other. // ManGS_2,1.10 //

children.text: dhāmno dhāmna iti tisṛbhiḥ parogoṣṭhaṃ mārjayante // ManGS_2,1.11 //
children.translated_text: With the three [verses] beginning with 'From abode to abode,' they purify themselves beyond the cowpen. // ManGS_2,1.11 //
Without looking back, they return. // ManGS_2,1.12 //
They efface the footprints with reeds or a branch of <s>vetasa</s> (cane)—

children.text: mṛtyoḥ padāni lopayante yadetaddrāghīrya āyuḥ pratiraṃ dadhānaḥ /
children.translated_text: They efface the footprints of death, thereby establishing long life.

children.text: āpyāyamānāḥ prajayā dhanena śuddhāḥ pūtā bhavantu yajñiyāsaḥ // ManGS_2,1.13 //
children.translated_text: Thriving with progeny and wealth, may they become pure, cleansed, and fit for sacrifice. // ManGS_2,1.13 //
Hold onto the bull as a raft, by which <s>Saramā</s> crossed over, calling out.
Thus. // ManGS_2,1.14 //
Having removed the fire-altar and sprinkled it, he lays down the earthly materials for the <s>agnyādheya</s> (fire-establishment), except for chaff and sand. // ManGS_2,1.15 //

children.text: araṇibhyāmagniṃ mathitvā hiraṇyaśakalaṃ ca nyupya prāgudayādupasthakṛto bhūriti jvalantamādadhāti // ManGS_2,1.16 //
children.translated_text: Having kindled fire from the fire-sticks and placed a gold fragment, before sunrise, having prepared the seat, he establishes [the fire] with '<s>Bhūḥ</s>' while it is blazing. // ManGS_2,1.16 //
A cow, a garment, and a bronze [vessel] are the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (sacrificial fee). // ManGS_2,1.17 //
Thus ends the first section of the second <s>puruṣa</s> (book). //1//
Second section.

children.text: prāgudañcaṃ lakṣaṇamuddhatyāvokṣya sthaṇḍilaṃ gomayenopalipyamaṇḍalaṃ caturasraṃvāgniṃ nirmathyābhimukhaṃ praṇayet // ManGS_2,2.1 //
children.translated_text: Having removed the mark [of the fire-altar] facing east and north, having sprinkled it, having smeared the ground with cow-dung, [making it] circular or square, having churned the fire, he should bring it facing [him]. // ManGS_2,2.1 //

children.text: darbhāṇāṃ pavitre mantravadutpādyāgneyaṃ sthālīpākaṃ śrapayati // ManGS_2,2.2 //
children.translated_text: Having ritually prepared the purifying [grass] with mantras, he cooks the <s>sthālīpāka</s> (oblation cooked in a pot) dedicated to <s>Agni</s>. // ManGS_2,2.2 //

children.text: pavitrāntarhite 'pa ānīya taṇḍulānopya mekṣaṇena pradakṣiṇaṃ paryāyuvañjīva taṇḍulaṃ śrapayati // ManGS_2,2.3 //
children.translated_text: Having brought water placed between the purifying [grasses], having put in the rice grains, stirring clockwise with the ladle [saying] 'Live long, O rice grain,' he cooks it. // ManGS_2,2.3 //

children.text: ghṛtenānutpūtena navanītena votpūtena śṛtamabhidhāryottarata udvāsayati // ManGS_2,2.4 //
children.translated_text: Having poured over it with ghee that has not been heated, or with fresh butter that has been heated, he sets it down to the north. // ManGS_2,2.4 //

children.text: imaṃ stomamarhata ityagniṃ parisamuhya paryukṣya paristīrya paścādagnerekavaddarhistṛṇāti // ManGS_2,2.5 //
children.translated_text: With 'Accept this hymn of praise,' having swept around the fire, having sprinkled around it, having strewn [grass] around it, he strews one layer of sacrificial grass behind the fire. // ManGS_2,2.5 //

Having drawn out the <s>darbha</s> grasses northward and eastward with tips, he strews [them] south of the fire with the northern [tips] facing forward, and the southern ones with the northern [ends] forward. // ManGS_2,2.6 //

children.text: dakṣiṇatognerbrāhmaṇe saṃstṛṇātyaparaṃ yajamānāya paścārddhe patnyai // ManGS_2,2.7 //
children.translated_text: South of the fire he strews [a seat] for the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> (priest); the next one for the sacrificer; in the western half, for the wife. // ManGS_2,2.7 //

children.text: uttarataḥ saṃstīrṇe pavitre sruksruvāvājyasthālīṃ prakṣālya saṃstīrṇe dve dve prayunakti // ManGS_2,2.8 //
children.translated_text: Having strewn the purifying [grasses] to the north, having washed the offering ladles and the ghee vessel on the strewn [grass], he yokes two by two. // ManGS_2,2.8 //

children.text: tūṣṇīṃ dakṣiṇata ājyaṃ nirūpya mantravatparyagniṃ kṛtvā tūṣṇīṃ sruksruvau saṃmṛjyādabdhena tvā cakṣuṣāvekṣa iti patnyājyāmavekṣate // ManGS_2,2.9 //
children.translated_text: Silently placing the ghee to the south, having made the circumambulation of the fire with mantras, silently wiping the ladles, the wife looks at the ghee with 'With an undeceived eye I look upon you.' // ManGS_2,2.9 //
Having silently placed [it] on the fire and then removed it, having brought it behind the fire and ritually purified it with mantras, he looks at it. // ManGS_2,2.10 //
The sacrificer looks at the ghee [saying] 'You are splendor.' // ManGS_2,2.11 //

children.text: ājyasthālyāṃ sruvaṃ nidhāyāgreṇa sthālīpākamanvāyātayatyapareṇa mekṣaṇam // ManGS_2,2.12 //
children.translated_text: Having placed the ladle in the ghee vessel, he extends [the offering] forward with the <s>sthālīpāka</s>, and the stirring spoon behind. // ManGS_2,2.12 //

children.text: tūṣṇīṃ prāñcamidhmamupasamādhāya brahmāṇamāmantrya oṃ juhudhītyukte dakṣiṇena hastenāntareṇa jānunī prāṅāsīna ādhārau juhoti prājāpatyamuttarārdhe prāñcaṃ manasā aindraṃ dakṣiṇārddhe prāñcameva // ManGS_2,2.13 //
children.translated_text: Silently having placed the fuel-stick forward, having addressed the <s>Brahman</s> (priest), when he says 'Om, make the offering,' sitting facing east between the knees with the right hand, he offers the two foundation oblations—the one for <s>Prajāpati</s> in the northern half facing forward, the one for <s>Indra</s> in the southern half likewise facing forward. // ManGS_2,2.13 //

children.text: athājyabhāgau juhotyāgneyamuttarārddhe saumyaṃ dakṣiṇārddhe samāvanakṣṇau // ManGS_2,2.14 //
children.translated_text: Then he offers the <s>ājyabhāgas</s> (ghee portions)—the one for <s>Agni</s> in the northern half, the one for <s>Soma</s> in the southern half, both meeting diagonally. // ManGS_2,2.14 //

children.text: yukto vaha yadākūtamiti dvābhyāmagniṃ yojayitvā nakṣatramiṣṭvā nakṣatradevatāṃ yajettithiṃ tithidevatāmṛtamṛtudevatāṃ ca // ManGS_2,2.15 //
children.translated_text: Having yoked <s>Agni</s> with the two [verses] 'Yoked, carry what is intended,' having worshipped the <s>nakṣatra</s> (constellation), he should sacrifice to the deity of the constellation, the <s>tithi</s> (lunar day), the deity of the lunar day, the <s>ṛtu</s> (season), and the deity of the season. // ManGS_2,2.15 //

children.text: upastīryāpa upaspṛśya mekṣaṇena sthālīpākasyāvadyati madhyāt pūrvārddhād dvitīyaṃ paścārddhāttṛtīyaṃ yadi pañcāvadānasya // ManGS_2,2.16 //
children.translated_text: Having spread [grass], having sipped water, he cuts off from the <s>sthālīpāka</s> with the ladle—from the middle, the second from the front half, the third from the back half, if it is a five-portion offering. // ManGS_2,2.16 //
Having poured [ghee] over what has been cut off, he pours [ghee] back over the <s>sthālīpāka</s>. // ManGS_2,2.27 //
He offers in the middle [saying] '<s>Agnaye svāhā</s>' (To <s>Agni</s>, hail!). // ManGS_2,2.18 //
'You who are of the gods'—for the <s>Raudra</s> (offering to <s>Rudra</s>). // ManGS_2,2.19 //
Having offered the <s>jaya</s> (victory) oblations, for the <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s> (the one who makes the offering successful) he cuts off from the northern half once, a double measure,
or twice, if it is a five-portion offering. // ManGS_2,2.20 //

children.text: avattaṃ dvirabhidhārya nāta urdhvaṃsthālīpākaṃ pratyabhidhārayati // ManGS_2,2.21 //
children.translated_text: Having poured [ghee] twice over what has been cut off, he does not pour [ghee] back over the <s>sthālīpāka</s> above that. // ManGS_2,2.21 //
He offers in the northeastern [part] without interruption, [saying] '<s>Agnaye sviṣṭakṛte svāhā</s>' (To <s>Agni</s> who makes the offering successful, hail!). // ManGS_2,2.22 //

children.text: mekṣaṇaṃ darbhāṃścādhāyānumatibhyāṃvyāhṛtibhiśca tvaṃ no agne, sa tvaṃ no agne
children.translated_text: Having placed the ladle and the <s>darbha</s> grasses, [he offers] with the <s>Anumati</s> [verses], with the <s>Vyāhṛtis</s>, and 'You, O <s>Agni</s>, for us,' 'That you, O <s>Agni</s>,'
'And <s>Agni</s>, you are'—with these he should offer. // ManGS_2,2.23 //

children.text: vi te muñcāmi raśanāṃ vi raśmīnīti ca dutvā pavitre 'nu prahṛtyājyenābhijuhoti // ManGS_2,2.24 //
children.translated_text: 'I release your cord, I release the reins'—having uttered this, having placed [them] on the purifying [grass], he makes a final offering with ghee. // ManGS_2,2.24 //

children.text: edho 'syedhīṣīmahīti samidhamādadhāti samidasi samedhiṣīmahīti dvitīyām // ManGS_2,2.25 //
children.translated_text: He places a fuel-stick [saying] 'You are fuel, may we be enkindled'; the second [saying] 'You are a fuel-stick, may we be enkindled.' // ManGS_2,2.25 //
He worships [saying] 'We have today followed the waters.' // ManGS_2,2.26 //
He should purify with the [verses] beginning with '<s>Āpo hi ṣṭhā</s>' (O waters, verily). // ManGS_2,2.27 //
A full vessel is the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (sacrificial fee). // ManGS_2,2.28 //
He throws out the sacrificial grass. // ManGS_2,2.29 //

children.text: etena sthālīpākena sthālīpākāḥ sarve vyākhyātāḥ // ManGS_2,2.30 //
children.translated_text: By this <s>sthālīpāka</s> (oblation cooked in a pot), all <s>sthālīpākas</s> are explained. // ManGS_2,2.30 //
Thus ends the second section of the second <s>puruṣa</s> (book). //2//
Third section.

children.text: agnaye svāheti sāyaṃ juhoti prajāpataya iti dvitīyām // ManGS_2,3.1 //
children.translated_text: He offers in the evening [saying] '<s>Agnaye svāhā</s>' (To <s>Agni</s>, hail!); the second [saying] 'To <s>Prajāpati</s>.' // ManGS_2,3.1 //

children.text: sūryāya svāheti prātaḥ prajāpataya iti dvitīyām // ManGS_2,3.2 //
children.translated_text: He offers in the morning [saying] '<s>Sūryāya svāhā</s>' (To <s>Sūrya</s>, hail!); the second [saying] 'To <s>Prajāpati</s>.' // ManGS_2,3.2 //

children.text: agnīṣomīyaḥ sthālīpākaḥ paurṇamāsyāmaindrāgno 'māvāsyāyāmubhayatra cāgneyaḥ āgantuḥ pūrvaḥ paurṇamāsyāmuttaromāvāsyāyām // ManGS_2,3.3 //
children.translated_text: The <s>sthālīpāka</s> dedicated to <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s> [is performed] on the full-moon day; [the one] dedicated to <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s> on the new-moon day; and [the one] dedicated to <s>Agni</s> on both occasions—the former first on the full-moon day, the latter on the new-moon day. // ManGS_2,3.3 //

children.text: āśvayujyāṃ paurṇamāsyāṃ pratarnityeṣu sthālīpākeṣu sthālīpākamanvāyātayati // ManGS_2,3.4 //
children.translated_text: On the full-moon day of <s>Āśvayuja</s> (autumn month), in the morning, among the regular <s>sthālīpākas</s>, he extends the <s>sthālīpāka</s>. // ManGS_2,3.4 //

children.text: tasyāgniṃrudraṃ paśupatimīśānaṃ tryambakaṃ śaradaṃ praṣātakaṃ gā iti yajati // ManGS_2,3.5 //
children.translated_text: For that [offering] he worships <s>Agni</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Paśupati</s>, <s>Īśāna</s>, <s>Tryambaka</s>, the autumn, the <s>praṣātaka</s> (offering cake), and the cattle. // ManGS_2,3.5 //

children.text: dadhighṛtamiśraḥ praṣātakastasyā no mitrāvaruṇā pravāhaveti ca hutvāmbhaḥ sthāmbho vo bhakṣīyeti gāḥ prāśāpayati // ManGS_2,3.6 //
children.translated_text: The <s>praṣātaka</s> is mixed with curds and ghee; having offered with 'May <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s> convey [this] for us,' [saying] 'Water, you are; may I partake of water,' he makes the cattle eat. // ManGS_2,3.6 //
And [the cattle] once released should dwell [freely]. // ManGS_2,3.7 //
He should feed <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> with ghee-mixed food. // ManGS_2,3.8 //
One should not eat of the new [grain] without having offered the <s>āgrayaṇa</s> (first-fruits offering). // ManGS_2,3.9 //

children.text: parvaṇyāgrayaṇaṃ kurvīta vasante yavānāṃ śaradi vrīhīṇām // ManGS_2,3.10 //
children.translated_text: He should perform the <s>āgrayaṇa</s> (first-fruits offering) on a <s>parvan</s> (sacred day)—of barley in spring, of rice in autumn. // ManGS_2,3.10 //

children.text: agrapākasya payasi sthālīpākaṃ śrapayitvā tasya juhoti sajūrdyāvāpṛthivībhyāṃ svāhā sajūḥ somāya svāheti // ManGS_2,3.11 //
children.translated_text: Having cooked the <s>sthālīpāka</s> in milk of the first-ripened [grain], he offers from it [saying] 'Together with heaven and earth, <s>svāhā</s>! Together with <s>Soma</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!' // ManGS_2,3.11 //

children.text: śaradi somāya śyāmākānāṃ vasanteveṇuyavānāmubhayatra vājyena // ManGS_2,3.12 //
children.translated_text: In autumn, [the offering] of <s>śyāmāka</s> (millet) for <s>Soma</s>; in spring, of bamboo barley—on both occasions with ghee. // ManGS_2,3.12 //
A first-born calf is the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (sacrificial fee). // ManGS_2,3.13 //

children.text: brāhmaṇa eva haviḥ śeṣaṃ bhujjīteti śrutiḥ // ManGS_2,3.14 //
children.translated_text: Only a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> should eat the remainder of the oblation—this is the <s>śruti</s> (sacred tradition). // ManGS_2,3.14 //
Thus ends the third section of the second <s>puruṣa</s> (book). //3//
Fourth section.
One who is about to sacrifice with an animal performs the <s>pākayajña</s> (domestic sacrifice) fire-ritual. // ManGS_2,4.1 //
As in the <s>paśubandha</s> (animal sacrifice), but silently, except for the deity-invocation oblation. // ManGS_2,4.2 //

children.text: prokṣyānumānyopapāyya paryagniṃ kṛtvā śāmitraṃ praṇīya vapāśrapaṇībhyāmudañcaṃ prakramamāṇamanvārabhante // ManGS_2,4.3 //
children.translated_text: Having sprinkled and consecrated [the animal], having made it drink, having circumambulated the fire, having brought forward the <s>śāmitra</s> (slaughtering fire), they take hold [of the animal] as it steps northward with the <s>vapāśrapaṇī</s> (omentum-roasting implements). // ManGS_2,4.3 //
He watches as [the animal] is being suffocated. // ManGS_2,4.4 //

children.text:
saṃjñaptaṃsnapayitvā yathādaivataṃ vapāmutkṛtya śrapayitvā'dhārāvājyabhāgau hutvā--jātavedo vapayā gaccha devāṃstvaṃhi hotā prathamo babhūva /
ghṛtasyāgne tanvā saṃbhava satyāḥ santu yajamānasya kāmāḥ svāhā /
iti
children.translated_text: Having bathed the suffocated [animal], having cut out the <s>vapā</s> (omentum) according to its deity, having roasted it, having offered the foundation oblations and ghee portions—'O <s>Jātavedas</s>, go to the gods with the omentum, for you were the first <s>hotṛ</s> (invoking priest). Be embodied in ghee, O <s>Agni</s>; may the desires of the sacrificer be true. <s>Svāhā</s>!'—thus
he offers the <s>vapā</s> (omentum). // ManGS_2,4.5 //
'<s>Svāhā</s>, <s>svāhā</s>'—[these are] the two surrounding [oblations]. // ManGS_2,4.6 //
He extends the <s>sthālīpāka</s> (oblation cooked in a pot) having the same deity as the animal. // ManGS_2,4.7 //
After that offering, the ghee portions [are offered]. // ManGS_2,4.8 //
The <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s> (offering for successful completion) is unspecified [as to deity]. // ManGS_2,4.9 //

children.text: pāśubandhikānāmavadānānāṃ rasasyāvadāya daivataiḥ pracarya vasāhomaśeṣeṇa diśaḥ pratijayati yathā vājinena vanaspatimājyasya // ManGS_2,4.10 //
children.translated_text: Having cut off portions of the <s>paśubandha</s> (animal sacrifice) offerings, having proceeded with the juice according to the deities, with the remainder of the <s>vapāhoma</s> (omentum oblation) he conquers the directions, as with the <s>vājin</s> (prize offering) [he offers] the <s>vanaspati</s> (lord of the forest) with ghee. // ManGS 2.4.10 //

children.text: jayān hutvā tryaṅgāṇāṃ sviṣṭakṛte samavadyati // ManGS_2,4.11 //
children.translated_text: Having offered the <s>jaya</s> (victory) oblations, he cuts off [portions] of the three-limbed [offerings] for the <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s> (offering for successful completion). // ManGS 2.4.11 //
The remainder is explained by the <s>sthālīpāka</s> (oblation cooked in a pot) [procedure]. // ManGS 2.4.12 //
For an animal [sacrifice], an animal itself is the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (sacrificial fee). // ManGS 2.4.13 //
Thus ends the fourth section of the second <s>puruṣa</s> (book). //4//
Fifth section.
The <s>Raudra</s> (offering to <s>Rudra</s>) [is performed] in autumn—the <s>śūlagava</s> (bull on a spit). // ManGS 2.5.1 //

children.text: prāgudīcyāṃ diśi grāmasyā sakāśe niśi gavāṃ madhye taṣṭo yūpaḥ // ManGS_2,5.2 //
children.translated_text: In the northeastern direction from the village, nearby, at night, in the midst of the cattle, [there should be] a hewn sacrificial post. // ManGS 2.5.2 //

children.text: prāk sviṣṭakṛto 'ṣṭhau śoṇitapuṭān namaste rudramanyava iti prabhṛtibhiraṣṭabhiranuvākairdikṣvantardikṣu copaharet // ManGS_2,5.3 //
children.translated_text: Before the <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s>, he should offer eight cups of blood in the [cardinal] directions and intermediate directions, with the eight <s>anuvākas</s> (sections) beginning with "<s>namaste rudra manyave</s>" ("Salutation to you, O <s>Rudra</s>, to your wrath"). // ManGS 2.5.3 //
He should not bring uncooked [meat] into the village. // ManGS 2.5.4 //
The remainder he should bury in the ground, including the hide. // ManGS 2.5.5 //
Some say that <s>pākayajña</s> (domestic sacrifice) animals [require] no sacrificial post. // ManGS 2.5.6 //
Thus ends the fifth section of the second <s>puruṣa</s>. //5//
Sixth section.
Now we shall explain the <s>Dhruvāśva</s> (permanent horse) rite. // ManGS 2.6.1 //
On the full-moon day of <s>Āśvayuja</s> (autumn month). // ManGS 2.6.2 //
The <s>ṛtvik</s> (officiating priest) should be without bodily defect, bathed, pure, wearing a new garment. // ManGS 2.6.3 //

children.text: prāgastamayānniṣkramyottarato grāmasya purastādvā śucau deśe 'śvatthasyādhastānnyagrodhasya vāpāṃ vā samīpe vedyakṛtiṃ kṛtvā tasyāṃ catuṣkoṇavanaspatiśākhāyāmasaktacīrāyāṃ gandhasragdāmavatyāṃ caturdiśaṃ vinyastodakummasahiraṇyabījapiṭikāyāmapūpasrastaralājollopikamaṅgalaphalākṣavatyāṃ sarvagandhasarvarasasarvauṣadhīḥ sarvaratnāni copakalpya pratisaradadhimadhumodakasvastikanandyāvartavatyāmagniṃ
children.translated_text: Having gone out before sunset, to the north of the village or in front of it, in a pure place, at the foot of an <s>aśvattha</s> (sacred fig) or <s>nyagrodha</s> (banyan) tree, or near water, having made a <s>vedi</s> (altar) shape, upon it [placing] a four-cornered tree branch with hanging bark strips, adorned with fragrant garlands, with water vessels placed in the four directions containing gold and seed-baskets, with cakes, garlands, parched grain, <s>ullopikā</s> (offerings), auspicious fruits, and <s>akṣa</s> (dice/beads), having prepared all fragrances, all flavors, all herbs, and all gems, and [having prepared an altar] with <s>pratisara</s> (protective thread), curds, honey, <s>modaka</s> (sweetmeats), <s>svastika</s> (auspicious marks), and <s>nandyāvarta</s> (auspicious designs), he brings the fire

children.text: praṇīyāśvatthapalāśakhadirarohitakodumbarāṇāmanyatamasyedhmamupasasādhāya tisraḥ pradhānadevatā yajatyuccaiḥśravasaṃ varuṇaṃ viṣṇumiti sthālīpākaiḥ paśubhiścāśvinau cāśvayujau cājyasya // ManGS_2,6.4 //
children.translated_text: forward; having arranged fuel of any one among <s>aśvattha</s> (sacred fig), <s>palāśa</s> (Butea frondosa), <s>khadira</s> (Acacia catechu), <s>rohitaka</s>, or <s>udumbara</s> (fig) [trees], he worships the three chief deities—<s>Uccaiḥśravas</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, and <s>Viṣṇu</s>—with <s>sthālīpākas</s> and animals; and the <s>Aśvins</s> and the [deities of] <s>Āśvayuja</s> [are worshipped] with ghee. // ManGS 2.6.4 //

children.text: jayān hutvā yā oṣadhayaḥ samannyāyanti punantu mā pitaro 'gnermanva iti caturbhiranuvākaurapo 'bhimantryāśvānsnapayati // ManGS_2,6.5 //
children.translated_text: Having offered the <s>jaya</s> (victory) oblations, with the four <s>anuvākas</s> beginning with "<s>yā oṣadhayaḥ</s>" ("Those herbs"), "may the ancestors purify me," "from <s>Agni</s>," having consecrated the waters, he bathes the horses. // ManGS 2.6.5 //

children.text: gandhasnagdāmabhiralaṃkṛtya pradakṣiṇaṃ devayajanaṃ triḥ pariyanti // ManGS_2,6.6 //
children.translated_text: Having adorned [them] with garlands of fragrance, they circumambulate the place of sacrifice three times from left to right. // ManGS 2.6.6 //
They cause [the horses] to rejoice. // ManGS 2.6.7 //
After the sacrifice, they go to their respective places. // ManGS 2.6.8 //
A cow and a bull are the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (sacrificial fee). // ManGS 2.6.9 //
Thus ends the sixth section of the second <s>puruṣa</s>. //6//
Seventh section.

children.text: āgrahāyaṇyāṃ paurṇamāsyāṃ payasi sthālīpākaṃ śrapayitvā tasya juhoti--
children.translated_text: On the full-moon day of <s>Āgrahāyaṇī</s> (Mārgaśīrṣa month), having cooked a <s>sthālīpāka</s> (oblation) in milk, he offers from it—
"The waters, white-footed, seizing, both from the east and from the west,

children.text: sapta ca vāruṇīrimāḥ prajāḥ sarvāśca rājabāndhavyaḥ svāhā //
children.translated_text: and these seven belonging to <s>Varuṇa</s>—[may] all these offspring and all the king's kinsmen [be blessed]. <s>Svāhā</s>!"

children.text: śveto ruṣatyo vidadhātyaśvo dadhadgarbhaṃ vṛṣaḥ satvaryāṃ jyok /
children.translated_text: "The white [one], the tawny one, dispenses; the horse bearing the embryo, the bull in the fertile cow, for a long time;
equally the people, wearing garments made by skill—you are the <s>Proṣādasa</s> <s>Savir</s>, all this."

children.text: śetāya rauṣiśvāya svāhā, na vai śvetasyābhyācāre ahirjaghāna kiṃcana /
children.translated_text: "To the white one, the son of <s>Ruṣiśvan</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! Verily, in the domain of the white one, no serpent has slain anything.
To the white one, the descendant of <s>Vaitāhavya</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!"
"May there be freedom from fear for us from the creatures of <s>Prajāpati</s>! <s>Svāhā</s>!"
Thus. // ManGS 2.7.1 //

children.text: srastare 'hataṃ vāsa udagdaśamāstīryodakāṃ vrīhīn yavānvāsya pariṣiñcati syonā pṛthivī bhaveti dvābhyāṃ sutrāmāṇamiti dvābhyām // ManGS_2,7.2 //
children.translated_text: On a spread [of grass], having spread a new garment facing north, having placed rice or barley with water toward the north, he sprinkles [with] the two [verses] "<s>syonā pṛthivī bhava</s>" ("Be gracious, O Earth") and the two [verses] "<s>sutrāmāṇam</s>" ("Well-protecting"). // ManGS 2.7.2 //

children.text: śamīśākhayā ca sapalāśayodañca triḥ samunmārṣṭi syonā pṛthivī bhaveti dvābhyāṃ sūtramāṇamiti dvābhyāṃ namo astu sarpebhya iti tisṛbhiśca // ManGS_2,7.3 //
children.translated_text: And with a <s>śamī</s> (Prosopis) branch with leaves, he sweeps northward three times [with] the two [verses] "<s>syonā pṛthivī bhava</s>," the two [verses] "<s>sūtramāṇam</s>," and the three [verses] "<s>namo astu sarpebhyaḥ</s>" ("Salutation to the serpents"). // ManGS 2.7.3 //

children.text:
śāmyantu sarpāḥ svaśayā bhavantu ye antarikṣa uta ye divi śritāḥ /
imāṃ mahīṃ pratyavarohema /
children.translated_text:
"May the serpents be at peace, resting in their own lairs—those who are in the atmosphere and those who dwell in heaven;
may we descend to this great earth,
auspicious, unceasing, peaceful, tranquil, with good winter, the best of the best years—may I accomplish this."
With this [verse] he installs [the beds], the eldest first, facing north. // ManGS 2.7.4 //

children.text: udīrghaṃ jīvo asurna āgādayaḥ prāgāttama ājyotireti /
children.translated_text: "He has risen up tall, like a living <s>Asura</s>; he who went forth before, that [darkness] has gone to light."

children.text: āraikapanthāṃ yātave sūryā-yāganmā yatna prataraṃ na āyuḥ /
children.translated_text: "Make way for the sun to travel on the single path; may we not go farther than our lifespan."
With this [verse], the youngest first, they rise up. // ManGS 2.7.5 //
On the full-moon day of <s>Caitra</s> (spring month) is the <s>udgroṇa</s> (rising up) [ceremony]. // ManGS 2.7.6 //

children.text: na tatra stālīpāko na śākhayā samunmārṣṭi // ManGS_2,7.7 //
children.translated_text: There is no <s>sthālīpāka</s> for that, nor sweeping with a branch. // ManGS 2.7.7 //

children.text: ayaṃ talpaḥ prataraṇo vasūnāṃ viśvārtvibhya(?) talpo asmān /
children.translated_text: "This couch is the means of crossing for the <s>Vasus</s>; [may] this couch [be] for all seasons for us;
may we live long with all our heroes, [on] that [couch]."
With this [mantra] the couch is consecrated. // ManGS 2.7.8 //
The three <s>nābhyāni</s> (navel-days, i.e., intercalary days) are on <s>Phālgunī</s>, <s>Āṣāḍhī</s>, and <s>Kārttikī</s> [full moons]. // ManGS 2.7.9 //
On those [days] one should not study [the Vedas]. // ManGS 2.7.10 //

children.text: tāsu payasi sthālīpākaḥ sa vyākhyātaḥ // ManGS_2,7.11 //
children.translated_text: On those [days] a <s>sthālīpāka</s> in milk [is offered]; that has been explained. // ManGS 2.7.11 //
Thus ends the seventh section of the second <s>puruṣa</s>. //7//
Eighth section.
There are three <s>Aṣṭakās</s> (eighth-day festivals). // ManGS 2.8.1 //
After <s>Āgrahāyaṇī</s> and before <s>Phālgunī</s>, the eighth days of the dark fortnights. // ManGS 2.8.2 //
On those [days] one should not study [the Vedas]. // ManGS 2.8.3 //

children.text: tāsu payasi sthālīpākaṃ śrapayitvā tasya juhoti--
children.translated_text: On those [days], having cooked a <s>sthālīpāka</s> in milk, he offers from it—
"O divine <s>Aṣṭakā</s>, you who are the waters, the supreme <s>tapas</s> (austerity), you are the means of release;

children.text: tvaṃ yajñe varuṇasyāvayā asi tasyai ta enā vidhema //
children.translated_text: you are the means of release in the sacrifice of <s>Varuṇa</s>; to you we offer these [oblations]."

children.text: ulūkhalā grāvāṇo ghoṣamakurvata haviḥ kṛṇvantaḥ parivatsarīyam
children.translated_text: "The mortars and pressing-stones raised a sound, preparing the oblation for the anniversary;

children.text: ekāṣṭake suprajasaḥ suvīrā jyogjīvema balihṛdo vayaṃ te //
children.translated_text: On the first <s>Aṣṭakā</s>, [may we be] blessed with good offspring and good heroes; may we live long, we who bring you offerings."
"The night which people welcome as she approaches, like a cow [giving milk],

children.text: saṃvatsarasya yā patnī sā no astu sumaṅgalī //
children.translated_text: she who is the wife of the year—may she be auspicious to us."
"Those who worship you, O night, as the image of the year,
may you unite their offspring, endowed with long life, with increase of wealth."
These four [verses] are for the <s>sthālīpāka</s>. // ManGS 2.8.4 //
"For the <s>Aṣṭakā</s>, for the generous giver"—
"<s>svāhā</s>" he appends everywhere. // ManGS 2.8.5 //

children.text: hemanto vasante grīṣmaṛtavaḥ śivānaḥ śivāno varṣā abhayāściraṃ naḥ vaiśvānaro 'dhiratiḥ prāṇādo no ahorātre kṛṇutāṃ dīrghamāyuḥ //
children.translated_text: "Winter, spring, and summer are the seasons; may they be auspicious to us; may the rains be auspicious and fearless for us for long; may <s>Vaiśvānara</s> (universal fire), the protector, giver of breath, and the days and nights make our lifespan long."

children.text: śāntā pṛthivī śivamantarikṣaṃ dyaur no devyabhayaṃ kṛṇotu /
children.translated_text: "May the earth be peaceful, the atmosphere auspicious; may the divine sky make us free from fear;

children.text: śivā diśaḥ pradiśa ādiśo na āpo vidyutaḥ paripāntvāyuḥ //
children.translated_text: may the auspicious directions, intermediate directions, and sub-directions protect our life from waters and lightning."

children.text: āpo marīcīḥ paripāntu viśvato dhātā samudro abhayaṃ kṛṇotu /
children.translated_text: "May the waters and rays protect [us] from all sides; may <s>Dhātṛ</s> and the ocean grant freedom from fear;

children.text: bhūtaṃ bhaviṣyaduta bhadramastu me brahmabhigūrttaṃ svarākṣāṇaḥ //
children.translated_text: may the past, the future, and the present be auspicious to me; may <s>Brahman</s> protect and <s>Svar</s> (heaven) shelter."

children.text: kaviragnirindraḥ somaḥ sūryo vāyurastu me agnirvaiśvānaro apahantu pāpam /
children.translated_text: "May the wise <s>Agni</s>, <s>Indra</s>, <s>Soma</s>, <s>Sūrya</s>, and <s>Vāyu</s> be for me; may <s>Agni</s> <s>Vaiśvānara</s> drive away evil;

children.text: bṛhaspatiḥ savitā śarma yacchatu śriyaṃ virājaṃ mayi pūṣā dadhātu //
children.translated_text: may <s>Bṛhaspati</s> and <s>Savitṛ</s> grant shelter; may <s>Pūṣan</s> bestow glory and sovereignty upon me."
These five [verses] are for the ghee [oblation]. // ManGS 2.8.6 //
Having offered the <s>jaya</s> oblations, [he says] "<s>iḍā</s>, O <s>Agni</s>"—thus for the <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s>. // ManGS 2.8.7 //
Thus for all [the Aṣṭakās]. // ManGS 2.8.8 //
Thus ends the eighth section of the second <s>puruṣa</s>. //8//
Ninth section.

children.text: uttamāyāḥ pradoṣe catuṣpathe 'ṅgaśo gāṃ kārayet // ManGS_2,9.1 //
children.translated_text: On the last [Aṣṭakā], in the evening, at a crossroads, he should have a cow cut up limb by limb. // ManGS 2.9.1 //

children.text: yo ya āgacchettasmai tasmai dadyāt // ManGS_2,9.2 //
children.translated_text: To whoever comes, to him he should give [a portion]. // ManGS 2.9.2 //
The next day he should have another [cow] slaughtered. // ManGS 2.9.3 //
Of its <s>vapā</s> (omentum) he should offer—

children.text: vaha vapāṃ jātavedaḥ pitṛbhyo yatraitānvettha nihitānparāke medaso ghṛtasya kulyā abhiniḥsravantu satyāḥ santu yajamānasya kāmāḥ svāhā /
children.translated_text: "Carry the omentum, O <s>Jātavedas</s>, to the ancestors, where you know them deposited far away; may streams of fat and ghee flow forth; may the desires of the sacrificer be true. <s>Svāhā</s>!"
Thus. // ManGS 2.9.4 //
Then with its breast he cooks rice facing north. // ManGS 2.9.5 //
The remainder is explained by the <s>Aṣṭakā</s> offering procedure. // ManGS 2.9.6 //
He cooks the remaining food. // ManGS 2.9.7 //

children.text: śvo 'vaśiṣṭaṃ bhaktaṃ randhayitvā piṇḍānāmāvṛtā trīnmāṃsaudanapiṇḍānnidadhāti // ManGS_2,9.8 //
children.translated_text: The next day, having cooked the remaining food, having turned around, he places three rice-and-meat balls (<s>piṇḍas</s>) among the [ancestor] offerings. // ManGS 2.9.8 //
He should give the <s>śrāddha</s> (ancestor offering) to the ancestors in the dark fortnight. // ManGS 2.9.9 //

children.text: anuguptamannaṃ brāhmaṇān bhojayen nāvedavidbhuñjīteti śrutiḥ // ManGS_2,9.10 //
children.translated_text: He should feed <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> with carefully guarded food; one who does not know the <s>Vedas</s> should not eat—thus is the <s>śruti</s>. // ManGS 2.9.10 //

children.text: yadi gavā paśunā vā kurvīta prokṣaṇamupapāyanaṃ paryagnikaraṇamulmukaharaṇaṃ vapāhomamiti // ManGS_2,9.11 //
children.translated_text: If he performs it with a cow or [other] animal, [the rites include] consecration by sprinkling, bringing near, circumambulation with fire, carrying of the firebrand, and the omentum oblation. // ManGS 2.9.11 //

children.text: traidhaṃ vapāṃ juhuyāt sthālīpākamavadānāni ca // ManGS_2,9.12 //
children.translated_text: He should offer the omentum in three portions, the <s>sthālīpāka</s>, and the cut portions. // ManGS 2.9.12 //
"To <s>Soma</s>, accompanied by the ancestors, <s>svadhā</s> (offering), salutation"—thus

children.text: juhoti yamāyāṅgirasvate pitṛmate svadhā nama iti dvitīyām /
children.translated_text: he offers; "To <s>Yama</s>, of the <s>Āṅgirasa</s> lineage, accompanied by the ancestors, <s>svadhā</s>, salutation"—the second;

children.text: agnaye kāvyavāhanāya svadhā nama iti tṛtīyām // ManGS_2,9.13 //
children.translated_text: "To <s>Agni</s>, the carrier of offerings to the sages, <s>svadhā</s>, salutation"—the third. // ManGS 2.9.13 //

children.text: evaṃ māsi māsi niyataṃ tantraṃ piṇḍapitṛyajñe // ManGS_2,9.14 //
children.translated_text: Thus month by month is the fixed procedure in the <s>piṇḍapitṛyajña</s> (offering of rice-balls to the ancestors). // ManGS 2.9.14 //
Thus ends the ninth section of the second [book]. //9//
Tenth section.

children.text: phālgunyāṃ paurṇamāsyāṃ purastāddhānāpūpābhyāṃ bhagaṃ cāryamaṇaṃca yajet // ManGS_2,10.1 //
children.translated_text: On the full-moon day of <s>Phālgunī</s>, beforehand, with two offerings of grain and cakes, he should worship <s>Bhaga</s> and <s>Aryaman</s>. // ManGS 2.10.1 //

children.text: indrāṇyā haviṣyān piṣṭvā piṣṭāni samutpūya yāvanti paśujātāni tāvato mithunān pratirūpān śrapayitvā kāṃsye 'dhyājyānkṛtvā tenaiva rudrāya svāheti /
children.translated_text: Having ground the sacrificial foods of <s>Indrāṇī</s>, having mixed the ground [substances], he prepares as many pairs in corresponding forms as there are kinds of animals; having prepared them, placing [them] anointed with ghee in a bronze [vessel], with the same [he offers saying] 'To <s>Rudra</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!'
'To <s>Īśāna</s>'—some [say]. // ManGS 2.10.2 //
In the evening he makes offerings with two cakes—to <s>Agni</s> and <s>Indra</s>. // ManGS 2.10.3 //

children.text: āgneyastundilo na tasya striyaḥ prāśnanti sarvāmātyā itarasya // ManGS_2,10.4 //
children.translated_text: The one dedicated to <s>Agni</s> is a <s>tuṇḍila</s> (round cake); the women do not eat of it; all the officials [eat] of the other. // ManGS 2.10.4 //
With a <s>sthālīpāka</s> [he worships] <s>Indrāṇī</s>—or <s>Śacī</s>. // ManGS 2.10.5 //
In combined [offerings], as in a single [offering]—the sacrificial grass, the fire, the foundation oblation, the ghee portions, the ghee oblations, and the <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s>. // ManGS 2.10.6 //

children.text: agnirindraḥ somaḥ sītā savitāsarasvatyaścinānumatī revatī rākā pūṣā rudra ityetairāyojana- paryayana-pravapana-pralava-sītāyajña-khalayajñatantīyajñānaḍudyajñeṣvetā devatā iti yajati sāṃvatsareṣu ca parvasu // ManGS_2,10.7 //
children.translated_text: <s>Agni</s>, <s>Indra</s>, <s>Soma</s>, <s>Sītā</s>, <s>Savitṛ</s>, <s>Sarasvatī</s>, the <s>Aśvins</s>, <s>Anumatī</s>, <s>Revatī</s>, <s>Rākā</s>, <s>Pūṣan</s>, <s>Rudra</s>—these are the deities in the yoking, driving, sowing, plowing, <s>Sītā</s>-sacrifice, threshing-floor sacrifice, weaving sacrifice, and bull sacrifice; and he worships these deities at the annual festivals. // ManGS 2.10.7 //
In rivers, oceans, wells, and tanks he worships <s>Varuṇa</s>; in herbs and trees, <s>Soma</s>; in those whose deity is unspecified, <s>Agni</s>. // ManGS 2.10.8 //
Thus ends the tenth section of the second [book]. //10//
Eleventh section.
The building site should be level, with [firm] foundation. // ManGS 2.11.1 //
A site sloping to the south [brings] desire for food; <s>Mārutas</s> (storm gods) dwell there, and offspring are born there. // ManGS 2.11.2 //
Water should drain off on all sides. // ManGS 2.11.3 //
Or one from which, having drained off, the waters would flow toward the northeast—that also [is suitable]. // ManGS 2.11.4 //

children.text: gartaṃ khātvā yattaiḥ pāṃsubhiḥ pratipūryeta tadvā // ManGS_2,11.5 //
children.translated_text: Or one where, having dug a pit, it would be refilled by the [same] soil—that also [is suitable]. // ManGS 2.11.5 //
If it would hold water [well]. // ManGS 2.11.6 //

children.text: idamahaṃ viśamannādyāya tejase brahmavarcasāya parigṛhṇāmīti veśma parigṛhya garte hiraṇya nidhāyācyutāya dhruvāya bhaumāya svāheti juhoti // ManGS_2,11.7 //
children.translated_text: "I take possession of this [site] for the people, for food, for splendor, for the radiance of sacred knowledge"—having taken possession of the house with this [mantra], having placed gold in the pit, he offers [saying] "To the immovable, the firm, the earthly one, <s>svāhā</s>!" // ManGS 2.11.7 //

children.text: samīcīnāmāsīti paryāyairupatiṣṭhate pratidiśaṃ dvābhyāṃ madhye // ManGS_2,11.8 //
children.translated_text: "Come together"—he approaches with the turns [of verses] in each direction, two [verses] per direction, [and one] in the middle. // ManGS 2.11.8 //

children.text: udakāṃsye 'śmānaṃ vrīhīnyavānvasya pariṣiñcati syonāpṛthivī bhaveti dvābhyāṃ
children.translated_text: In a water vessel [he places] a stone, rice, and barley, and sprinkles [with] the two [verses] "<s>syonā pṛthivī bhava</s>" ("Be gracious, O Earth")
and the two [verses] "<s>sutrāmāṇam</s>" ("Well-protecting"). // ManGS 2.11.9 //

children.text: śamīśākhayā ca palāśayodañcaṃ triḥ samunmārṣṭi syonā prathivi bhaveti dvābhyāṃ sutramāṇamiti dvābhyāṃ namo astu sarpebhya iti tisṛbhiśca // ManGS_2,11.10 //
children.translated_text: And with a <s>śamī</s> branch with leaves, he sweeps northward three times [with] the two [verses] "<s>syonā pṛthivī bhava</s>," the two [verses] "<s>sutrāmāṇam</s>," and the three [verses] "<s>namo astu sarpebhyaḥ</s>" ("Salutation to the serpents"). // ManGS 2.11.10 //
"This is entirely auspicious on all sides; this is vigor, this is essence;
having attained human desires thus, that headless one will obtain [all]."

children.text: iti madhyamāṃ sthūṇāmāsicya garta āsiñcati // ManGS_2,11.11 //
children.translated_text: With this [verse], having anointed the central pillar, he pours [the offering] into the pit. // ManGS 2.11.11 //

children.text:
ihaiva tiṣṭha nitarā tilvalā sthirāvati /
madhye poṣasya puṣpatāmā tvā parisṛtaḥ kumbhaḥ /
children.translated_text:
"Stand right here firmly, O <s>Tilvalā</s>, with firm foundation;
in the midst of nourishment may you flourish; may the full pot surround you;

children.text: ā vatse jagato saha ā dadhnaḥ kalaśamairayam //
children.translated_text: may the calf come with the world, and may I raise the pot of curds."
With this [verse] the central pillar is consecrated. // ManGS 2.11.12 //

children.text: vasūnāṃ tvā vasuvīryasyāhorātrayośceti garte sthūṇāmavadadhāti // ManGS_2,11.13 //
children.translated_text: "Of the <s>Vasus</s>, for you, of the vigor of the <s>Vasus</s>, of day and night"—[saying] this, he places the pillar in the pit. // ManGS 2.11.13 //
"Without a pillar, mount the beam rightly, O <s>Agni</s>; approach <s>Virāj</s>, impel <s>Śakra</s> (Indra)."
With this [verse] he places the central beam. // ManGS 2.11.14 //
The remaining pillars and beams [are placed] silently. // ManGS 2.11.15 //

children.text: prāgdvāraṃ dakṣiṇādvāraṃ vā māpayitvā gṛhānahaṃ sumanasaḥ prapadye vīraṃ hītyetayā prapadyate yathā purastādvyākhyātam // ManGS_2,11.16 //
children.translated_text: Having measured [the house] with a door facing east or facing south, "I approach the houses with good mind, with heroes"—with this [verse] he enters, as previously explained. // ManGS 2.11.16 //
"The king <s>Varuṇa</s>, the foremost traveler, with the <s>Revatīs</s> (wealthy stars), may he stand in this place, being nourished;

children.text: irāṃ vahantī ghṛtamukṣamāṇāsteṣvahaṃ sumanāḥ saṃ vasāma //
children.translated_text: bearing nourishment, anointed with ghee—in those [houses] may we dwell with happy minds."
With this [verse] he places a water pot for drinking in the northeastern direction. // ManGS 2.11.17 //
"I send you forth to the ocean; go to your own source;

children.text: ariṣṭā asmākaṃ vīrā mā parāseci matpayaḥ /
children.translated_text: may our heroes be unharmed; let not my milk be spilled."
With this [verse], the draining [channel is directed] northward. // ManGS 2.11.18 //

children.text:
vāstoṣpatyaṃ payasi sthālīpākaṃ śrapayitvā tasya juhoti /
amīvahā vāstoṣpate vāstoṣpata ityetābhyām-
children.translated_text: Having cooked a <s>sthālīpāka</s> (oblation) in milk for <s>Vāstoṣpati</s> (Lord of the dwelling), he offers from it, with the two [verses] "<s>amīvahā Vāstoṣpate</s>" ("O <s>Vāstoṣpati</s>, destroyer of disease") and "<s>Vāstoṣpate</s>"—

children.text:
vāstoṣpate prataraṇo na adhi gayasphāno gobhiraśvebhirindo
ajarāsaste sakhye vyāma piteva putrānprati no juṣasva //
children.translated_text: O <s>Vāstoṣpati</s> (lord of the dwelling), be our promoter, increaser of prosperity, rich in cattle and horses, O <s>Indra</s>; unaging in your friendship, may we abide; accept us as a father [accepts] his sons.

children.text: vāstoṣpate śagmayā saṃ sadā te sakṣīmahi raṇavayā gātumatyā pāhi kṣema uta yoge varaṃ no yūyaṃ pāta svastibhiḥ sadā naḥ //
children.translated_text: O <s>Vāstoṣpati</s>, may we dwell in your pleasant, joyful, and gracious [abode]; protect us in security and in activity; grant us the best. O you [gods], protect us always with blessings.
Thus. // ManGS_2,11.19 //
The rest is the same beginning with the <s>jaya</s> (victory oblations). // ManGS_2,11.20 //
Thus ends the eleventh section of the second [book]. //11//
Twelfth section.

children.text: vaiśvadevasya siddhasya sāyaṃ prātarbaliṃ haret // ManGS_2,12.1 //
children.translated_text: He should offer the <s>bali</s> (food offering) of the cooked <s>vaiśvadeva</s> (offering to all gods) in the evening and morning. // ManGS_2,12.1 //

children.text: agnīṣomau dhanvantariṃ viśvāndevānprajāpatimagniṃ sviṣṭakṛtamityevaṃ homo vidhīyate // ManGS_2,12.2 //
children.translated_text: The <s>homa</s> (fire oblation) is prescribed thus: to <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s>, to <s>Dhanvantari</s>, to all the gods, to <s>Prajāpati</s>, and to <s>Agni Sviṣṭakṛt</s>. // ManGS_2,12.2 //

children.text: atha baliṃ haratyagnaye namaḥ somāya dhanvantaraye viśvebhyo devebhyaḥ prajāpataye agnaye sviṣṭakṛta ityagnyāgāra uttarāmuttarām // ManGS_2,12.3 //
children.translated_text: Then he offers the <s>bali</s>: 'Homage to <s>Agni</s>, to <s>Soma</s>, to <s>Dhanvantari</s>, to all the gods, to <s>Prajāpati</s>, to <s>Agni Sviṣṭakṛt</s>'—each successively further north in the fire-house. // ManGS_2,12.3 //
'To the waters'—near the water-jar. // ManGS_2,12.4 //

children.text: oṣadhibhya ityoṣadhibhyo vanaspatibhya iti gṛhamadhyamāyāṃ sthūṇāyām // ManGS_2,12.5 //
children.translated_text: 'To the herbs'—to the herbs; 'to the trees'—at the central pillar of the house. // ManGS_2,12.5 //
'To the domestic deities'—in the middle of the house. // ManGS_2,12.6 //
'To <s>Dharma</s> (righteousness), to <s>Adharma</s> (unrighteousness)'—at the door. // ManGS_2,12.7 //
'To <s>Mṛtyu</s> (death), to the sky'—in the open air. // ManGS_2,12.8 //
'To the interior of the cow-pen'—inside the cow-pen. // ManGS_2,12.9 //
'To <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> (Kubera) on the sacrificial grass'—outside to the east. // ManGS_2,12.10 //
'To all the gods'—in the dwelling. // ManGS_2,12.11 //
'To <s>Indra</s> and <s>Indra's</s> attendants'—in front. // ManGS_2,12.12 //
'To <s>Yama</s> and <s>Yama's</s> attendants'—to the south. // ManGS_2,12.13 //
'To <s>Varuṇa</s> and <s>Varuṇa's</s> attendants'—to the west. // ManGS_2,12.14 //
'To <s>Soma</s> and <s>Soma's</s> attendants'—to the north. // ManGS_2,12.15 //
'To <s>Brahman</s> and <s>Brahman's</s> attendants'—in the middle. // ManGS_2,12.16 //

children.text: prācīmāpātikebhyaḥ sampātikebhya ṛkṣebhyo yakṣebhyaḥ pipīlikābhyaḥ piśācebhyo 'psarobhyo gandharvebhyo guhyakebhyaḥ śailebhyaḥ pannagebhyaḥ // ManGS_2,12.17 //
children.translated_text: To the east: to the <s>āpātikas</s> (those who fall upon), <s>sampātikas</s> (those who fly together), <s>ṛkṣas</s> (bears/stars), <s>yakṣas</s>, ants, <s>piśācas</s> (demons), <s>apsarases</s> (celestial nymphs), <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>guhyakas</s> (hidden beings), mountain [spirits], and serpents. // ManGS_2,12.17 //

children.text: divācāribhyo bhūtebhya iti divā naktaṃ cāribhyo bhūtebhya iti naktam // ManGS_2,12.18 //
children.translated_text: 'To the beings that wander by day'—during the day; 'to the beings that wander by night'—at night. // ManGS_2,12.18 //
The offering of satisfaction to <s>Dhanvantari</s>. // ManGS_2,12.19 //

children.text: adbhiḥ saṃsṛjya pitṛbhyaḥ svadheti śeṣaṃ dakṣiṇā bhūmau ninayet // ManGS_2,12.20 //
children.translated_text: Having mixed with water, [saying] 'To the ancestors, <s>svadhā</s> (offering to the dead),' he should place the remainder on the ground to the south. // ManGS_2,12.20 //
Having washed his hands and sipped water, having fed a guest, he should eat of the remainder. // ManGS_2,12.21 //
Thus ends the twelfth section of the second <s>puruṣa</s> (book). //12//
Thirteenth section.
Now we shall explain the <s>ṣaṣṭhīkalpa</s> (rite of the sixth day). // ManGS_2,13.1 //
On the fifth [day] of the bright fortnight, facing west, he should eat food suitable for offering. // ManGS_2,13.2 //

children.text: adhaḥ śayīta darbheṣu śālīpalāleṣu vā prākśirā brahmacārī // ManGS_2,13.3 //
children.translated_text: He should sleep below on <s>darbha</s> grass or rice straw, with his head to the east, observing <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibacy). // ManGS_2,13.3 //

children.text: śvobhūta udita āditye snānaṃ pānaṃ bhojanamanulepanaṃ srajo vāsāṃsi na pratyācakṣīta // ManGS_2,13.4 //
children.translated_text: The next day, after the sun has risen, he should not refuse bathing, drinking, eating, anointing, garlands, or garments. // ManGS_2,13.4 //
He should eat as much as is given; whatever is given, he should eat—except [food from] impure persons and those guilty of grave sins, which should be avoided. // ManGS_2,13.5 //
After the sun has set, having cooked a <s>sthālīpāka</s> in milk, he offers with these names:
The giver of wealth, rich in treasures, sovereign, fulfiller of desires for all who desire,

children.text: puṇyāṃ yaśasvinīṃ devīṃ ṣaṣṭhīṃ śakra juṣasva me //
children.translated_text: the auspicious, glorious goddess <s>Ṣaṣṭhī</s>—O <s>Śakra</s> (Indra), be pleased with me.

children.text:
nandī bhūtiśca lakṣmīścādityā ca yaśasvinī
sumanā vāk ca siddhiśca ṣaṣṭhī me diśatāṃ dhanam //
children.translated_text: Joy, prosperity, <s>Lakṣmī</s>, <s>Ādityā</s>, the glorious one, <s>Sumanā</s>, Speech, and <s>Siddhi</s>—may <s>Ṣaṣṭhī</s> grant me wealth.

children.text:
putrānpaśūndhanaṃ dhānyaṃ bahvaścājagaveḍakam
manasā yatpraṇītaṃ ca tanme diśatu havyabhuk //
children.translated_text: Sons, cattle, wealth, grain, many [animals]—goats and sheep—and whatever is conceived in the mind, may the oblation-eater grant me that.

children.text:
kānadāṃ rajanīṃ viśvarūpāṃ ṣaṣṭhīmupavarttatu me dhanam
sāma kāma kāmapatnī ṣaṣṭhī me diśatāṃ dhanam //
children.translated_text: May <s>Ṣaṣṭhī</s>, the giver of desires, nocturnal, of universal form, turn wealth toward me; O <s>Sāma</s>, O <s>Kāma</s>, O wife of <s>Kāma</s>, may <s>Ṣaṣṭhī</s> grant me wealth.

children.text: ākṛtiḥ prakṛtivarcanī dhāvaniḥ padmacāriṇī manmanā bhava svāhā //
children.translated_text: Form, primordial nature, splendor, speed, lotus-walker—be favorable to me, <s>svāhā</s>!

children.text:
gandhadvārāṃ durādharṣāṃ nityapuṣṭāṃ karīṣiṇīm
īśvarīṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ tāmihopahvaye śriyam /
children.translated_text: Her whose gateway is fragrance, who is indomitable, ever-nourished, and abounding in wealth, the sovereign of all beings—that <s>Śrī</s> (prosperity) I invoke here.

children.text:
nānāpatrakā (ka) sā devī puṣṭiścātisarasvatī
ariṃ devīṃ prapadyeyamupavarttayatu me dhanam //
children.translated_text: That goddess of various leaves, and <s>Puṣṭi</s> (nourishment), and most <s>Sarasvatī</s>—I take refuge in the goddess; may she turn wealth toward me.
O goddess of golden ramparts, come to me as the best; may life and glory [come], <s>svāhā</s>!
Filled with horses, centered on chariots, delighting in the trumpeting of elephants,
I invoke the goddess <s>Śrī</s>; may the divine <s>Śrī</s> be pleased with me.
May the hosts of gods and snakes come to me, together with <s>tapas</s> (austerity);

children.text: prādurbhūto 'smi rāṣṭre 'smin śrīḥ śraddhāṃ (kīrtiṃ vṛddhiṃ ga. ca.) dadhātu me //
children.translated_text: I have manifested in this kingdom; may <s>Śrī</s> bestow faith (fame, growth) upon me.

children.text: śriyai svāhā, hriyai svāhā, lakṣmyai svāhā, upalakṣmyai svāhā, nanhāyai svāhā, haridrāyai svāhā, ṣaṣṭhyai svāhā, samṛddhyai svāhā, jayāyai svāhā, kāmāyai svāheti // ManGS_2,13.6 //
children.translated_text: To <s>Śrī</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! To <s>Hrī</s> (modesty), <s>svāhā</s>! To <s>Lakṣmī</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! To <s>Upalakṣmī</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! To <s>Nandā</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! To <s>Haridrā</s> (turmeric), <s>svāhā</s>! To <s>Ṣaṣṭhī</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! To <s>Samṛddhi</s> (abundance), <s>svāhā</s>! To <s>Jayā</s> (victory), <s>svāhā</s>! To <s>Kāmā</s> (desire), <s>svāhā</s>! // ManGS_2,13.6 //
The rest is the same beginning with the <s>jaya</s> (victory oblations). // ManGS_2,13.7 //
He should observe [this rite] for six months, or three [months], on both fortnights. // ManGS_2,13.8 //
The combination [yields] a hundred thousand, or [the rite is performed] once. // ManGS_2,13.9 //
A cow and a bull are the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (sacrificial fee). // ManGS_2,13.10 //
Thus ends the thirteenth section of the second [book]. //13//
Fourteenth section.
Now we shall explain the <s>Vināyakas</s> (obstructors). // ManGS_2,14.1 //
They are <s>Śālakaṭaṅkaṭa</s>, <s>Kūṣmāṇḍarājaputra</s>, <s>Usmita</s>, and <s>Devayajana</s>. // ManGS_2,14.2 //
These are the signs of those afflicted by them: // ManGS_2,14.3 //
He crushes a clod of earth. // ManGS_2,14.4 //
He cuts grass. // ManGS_2,14.5 //
He scratches lines on his limbs. // ManGS_2,14.6 //
He sees bad dreams. // ManGS_2,14.7 //
He sees shaven-headed [persons]. // ManGS_2,14.8 //
He sees persons with matted hair. // ManGS_2,14.9 //
He sees persons wearing ochre robes. // ManGS_2,14.10 //
He sees camels, boars, donkeys, mad persons, and other impure [beings] in dreams. // ManGS_2,14.11 //
He traverses the sky [in dreams]. // ManGS_2,14.12 //

children.text: adhvānaṃ vrajanmanyate pṛṣṭhato me kaścidanuvrajati // ManGS_2,14.13 //
children.translated_text: While walking on a path, he thinks: 'Someone is following me from behind.' // ManGS_2,14.13 //

children.text: etaiḥ khaluvināyakairāviṣṭā rājaputrā lakṣaṇavanto rājyaṃ na labhante // ManGS_2,14.14 //
children.translated_text: Princes who are afflicted by these <s>Vināyakas</s>, though possessing [auspicious] marks, do not obtain kingship. // ManGS_2,14.14 //

children.text: kanyāḥ patikāmā lakṣaṇavatyo bhartṝnna labhante // ManGS_2,14.15 //
children.translated_text: Maidens desiring husbands, though possessing [auspicious] marks, do not obtain husbands. // ManGS_2,14.15 //

children.text: striyaḥ prajākāmā lakṣaṇavatyaḥ prajāṃ na labhante // ManGS_2,14.16 //
children.translated_text: Women desiring offspring, though possessing [auspicious] marks, do not obtain progeny. // ManGS_2,14.16 //
The children of virtuous women die. // ManGS_2,14.17 //
A learned teacher does not attain the status of <s>ācārya</s> (preceptor). // ManGS_2,14.19 //
Great obstacles arise in the studies of students. // ManGS_2,14.19 //
The trade routes of merchants are destroyed. // ManGS_2,14.20 //
The farming of cultivators yields meager results. // ManGS_2,14.21 //
For them, the <s>prāyaścitta</s> (expiation) [is as follows]: // ManGS_2,14.22 //
[One should prepare] earth from an animal burrow, <s>gorocanā</s> (yellow pigment from cattle), and <s>guggulu</s> (bdellium resin). // ManGS_2,14.23 //
He should bring four complete water-jars from four springs. // ManGS_2,14.24 //
He should prepare all fragrances, all flavors, all herbs, all gems, along with a protective thread, curds, honey, and ghee. // ManGS_2,14.25 //
Having mixed these ingredients, mounting on a bull's hide, then [he should bathe] him—
Thousand-eyed, hundred-streamed, made purifying by the sages,
with these [waters] I consecrate you; may the purifying [verses] cleanse you.

children.text: agninā dattā, indreṇa dattā, somena dattā, varuṇena dattā, vāyunā dattā,viṣṇunā dattā bṛhaspatinā dattā, viśvairdevairdattaḥ, sarvairdevairdattā oṣadhaya āpo varuṇasaṃmitāstābhiṣṭvābhiṣiñcāmi pāvamānīḥ punantu tveti
children.translated_text: Given by <s>Agni</s>, given by <s>Indra</s>, given by <s>Soma</s>, given by <s>Varuṇa</s>, given by <s>Vāyu</s>, given by <s>Viṣṇu</s>, given by <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, given by all the <s>Devas</s>, given by all the gods—the herbs and waters sanctioned by <s>Varuṇa</s>—with these I consecrate you; may the purifying [verses] cleanse you—
he adds everywhere—

children.text: yatte keśeṣu dairbhāgyaṃ sīmante tatra mūrddhani /
children.translated_text: Whatever misfortune is in your hair, at the parting, there on the crown of the head,
at the forehead, at the ears, at the eyes—may the waters [remove it] from you always.

children.text: bhagaṃ te varuṇe rājā bhra---sūryo bṛhaspatiḥ /
children.translated_text: King <s>Varuṇa</s> [has given you] fortune, <s>Sūrya</s> [and] <s>Bṛhaspati</s> [have given] splendor,
<s>Indra</s> and <s>Vāyu</s> and the seven sages have given [you] fortune.
Thus. // ManGS_2,14.26 //

children.text: adhista--- niśāyāṃ sadyaḥ pīḍitasarṣapatailamamaudumbareṇa sruveṇa --- catasra āhutirjuhoti (oṃ) śālakaṭaṅkaṭāya sva-- kūṣmāḍarājaputrāya svāhā, usmitāya svāhā, devayajanāyā svāheti // ManGS_2,14.27 //
children.translated_text: Having stood... at night, immediately, with mustard oil pressed, with an <s>audumbara</s> (fig-wood) ladle, he offers four oblations: 'To <s>Śālakaṭaṅkaṭa</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! To <s>Kūṣmāṇḍarājaputra</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! To <s>Usmita</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! To <s>Devayajana</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!' // ManGS_2,14.27 //

children.text: ata ūrdhvaṃ grāmacatuṣpathe nagaracatuṣpathe nigamacatuṣpathe sarvatomukhāndarbhānāstīrya nave śūrpe balimupaharati phalīkṛtāṃstaṇḍulānaphalīkṛtāṃstaṇḍulānāmaṃ māṃsaṃ pakvaṃ māṃsamāmānmatsyānpakvānmatsyān āmānapūpānpakvānapūpānpiṣṭāngandhānapiṣṭāngandhā---- madhupānaṃ maireyapānaṃ surāpānaṃ muktaṃ mālyaṃ grathithaṃ mālyaṃ raktaṃ mālyaṃ śuklaṃ mālyaṃ raktapītaśuklakṛṣṇanīlaharitacitravāsāṃsi mākalmāṣamūlabhalamiti // ManGS_2,14.28 //
children.translated_text: After that, at a village crossroads, a city crossroads, or a market crossroads, having spread <s>darbha</s> grass in all directions, he offers a <s>bali</s> (food offering) on a new winnowing basket: husked rice grains, unhusked rice grains, raw meat, cooked meat, raw fish, cooked fish, raw cakes, cooked cakes, ground fragrances, unground fragrances, honey-drink, <s>maireya</s> (liquor), <s>surā</s> (wine), loose garlands, bound garlands, red garlands, white garlands, garments of red, yellow, white, black, blue, green, and variegated colors, roots and fruits of the <s>mākalmāṣa</s> plant. // ManGS_2,14.28 //

children.text: atha devānāmāvāhanaṃ vimukhaḥ śeyeno bako yakṣaḥ kalaho bhīrurvināyakaḥ kūṣmāṇḍarā---- yajñāvikṣepī kulaṅgāpamāro yūpakeśī sūparakroḍī haimavato, jambhako virūpākṣo lohitākṣo vaiśravaṇo mahāseno mahādevo mahārāja iti /
children.translated_text: Then the invocation of the deities: <s>Vimukha</s>, <s>Śyena</s>, <s>Baka</s>, <s>Yakṣa</s>, <s>Kalaha</s>, <s>Bhīru</s>, <s>Vināyaka</s>, <s>Kūṣmāṇḍarāja</s>..., the one who disrupts sacrifices, <s>Kulaṅga</s>, <s>Apamāra</s>, <s>Yūpakeśī</s>, <s>Sūparakroḍī</s>, <s>Haimavata</s>, <s>Jambhaka</s>, <s>Virūpākṣa</s>, <s>Lohitākṣa</s>, <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>, <s>Mahāsena</s>, <s>Mahādeva</s>, <s>Mahārāja</s>.

children.text: ete me devāḥ prīyantāṃ prītā māṃ prīṇayantu tṛptā māṃ tarpayantviti // ManGS_2,14.29 //
children.translated_text: May these gods be pleased with me; being pleased, may they gratify me; being satisfied, may they satisfy me. // ManGS_2,14.29 //
At midnight, standing, the <s>ācārya</s> (teacher) worships the planets:

children.text: bhagavati bhagaṃ me dedi, varṇavati varṇaṃ me dehi, rūpavati rūpaṃ me dehi, tejasvini tejo me dehi, yaśasvini yaśo me dehi, putravati putrānme dehi, sarvavati sarvānkāmānme pradehīti // ManGS_2,14.30 //
children.translated_text: O fortunate one, give me fortune; O beautiful one, give me beauty; O graceful one, give me grace; O radiant one, give me radiance; O glorious one, give me glory; O mother of sons, give me sons; O possessor of all, grant me all desires. // ManGS_2,14.30 //

children.text: ata ūrdhvamudita āditye vimale sumuhūrtte sūryapūjāpūrvakamardhyadānamupasthānaṃ ca--
children.translated_text: After that, when the sun has risen, at an auspicious and clear moment, preceded by sun-worship, [he performs] the <s>arghya</s> (offering of water) and <s>upasthāna</s> (reverential standing)—

children.text: namaste astu bhagavan śataraśme tamonuda jahi me deva daurbhagyaṃ saubhāgyena māṃ saṃyojayasva //
children.translated_text: Salutations to you, O blessed one of hundred rays, dispeller of darkness; O god, destroy my misfortune and unite me with good fortune.
Thus. // ManGS_2,14.31 //
Then the satisfaction of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>. // ManGS_2,14.32 //
A bull is the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (sacrificial fee). // ManGS_2,14.33 //
Thus ends the fourteenth section of the second [book]. //14//
Fifteenth section.

children.text: yadi duḥsvapnaṃ paśyedvyāhṛtibhistilān hutvā diśā upatiṣṭhet /
children.translated_text: If one sees a bad dream, having offered sesame seeds with the <s>Vyāhṛtis</s>, he should worship the directions:
'May Awakening and Counter-awakening protect me from the east;
may Sleeplessness and Undrowsiness protect me from the south.'

children.text: gopāyamānaṃ ca māṃ rakṣamāṇaṃ ca paścād gopāyatām /
children.translated_text: 'May [they] who guard and protect me guard me from the west;
may the Watchful One and <s>Arundhatī</s> protect me from the north.'
May <s>Viṣṇu</s> and the Earth and the Serpents protect me from below;

children.text: bṛhaspatayaśca me viśve ca me devā dyauścopariṣṭhādgopāyatām // ManGS_2,15.1 //
children.translated_text: may <s>Bṛhaspati</s> and all the gods and Heaven protect me from above. // ManGS_2,15.1 //
Likewise, whenever any calamity arises and one apprehends misfortune. // ManGS_2,15.2 //

children.text: vyāhṛtibhistilān hutvā tapaḥ pratipadyeta dvādaśarātraṃ ṣaḍrātraṃ trirātramokarātraṃ vā // ManGS_2,15.3 //
children.translated_text: Having offered sesame seeds with the <s>Vyāhṛtis</s>, he should undertake <s>tapas</s> (austerity) for twelve nights, six nights, three nights, or one night. // ManGS_2,15.3 //
Or if he considers it a portent, [he should do] the same. // ManGS_2,15.4 //

children.text: yadi parvasu mārtikaṃ bhidyate pārthivamāsi pṛthivīṃ dṛṃhasva yoniṃ gaccha svāhetyapsu praharet // ManGS_2,15.5 //
children.translated_text: If an earthen [vessel] breaks on sacred days, [saying] 'You are earthen, make the earth firm, go to your source, <s>svāhā</s>,' he should cast [the pieces] into water. // ManGS_2,15.5 //

children.text:
yadyarcā dahyedvā naśyedvā prapatedvā prabhajedvā prahasedvā pracaledvā, sthālyā vā sthālīmāsicya dakṣiṇottarā vā sthālī bhidyetottarā vopalāśe niyamya dvāravaṃśo vā sphuṭet /
gaur vā gāṃ dhayet, strī vā striyamāhanyāt, kartasaṃsarge , halasaṃsarge, musalaprapatane, musalaṃvāvaśīryetānyasmiṃścādbhuta etābhirjuhuyāt--
children.translated_text: If the sacred fire burns, is destroyed, falls, breaks, laughs, or trembles; or if one pot overflows into another, or the southern or northern pot breaks, or if an obstacle is placed on the northern side, or if the door-post splits; or if a cow suckles [another] cow, or a woman strikes a woman, or there is contact with a pit, or contact with a plough, or falling of a pestle, or if a pestle crumbles, or any other portent—with these [mantras] he should offer:

children.text:
svasti na indro vṛddhaśravāḥ svastinaḥ pūṣā viśvavedāḥ /
svasti nastārkṣyo ariṣṭanemiḥ svastino bṛhaspatirdadhātu /
children.translated_text: May <s>Indra</s> of great fame grant us well-being; may <s>Pūṣan</s>, the all-knowing, [grant us] well-being; may <s>Tārkṣya</s> of unbroken rim [grant us] well-being; may <s>Bṛhaspati</s> bestow well-being upon us.

children.text: svasti no mimītāmāśvinā bhagaḥ svasti devyaditiranarvaṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: May the <s>Aśvins</s> grant us well-being, may <s>Bhaga</s> [grant us] well-being; may the divine <s>Aditi</s> [grant us] well-being, she who is without flaw.

children.text: svasti pūṣā asuro dadhātu naḥ svastidyāvāpṛthivī sucetunā //
children.translated_text: May <s>Pūṣan</s>, the <s>Asura</s>, bestow well-being upon us; may Heaven and Earth [grant us] well-being with good understanding.

children.text: svastaye vāyumupabravāmahai somaṃ svasti bhuvanasya yaspatiḥ /
children.translated_text: For well-being we invoke <s>Vāyu</s>; <s>Soma</s>, who is the lord of the world, for well-being;

children.text: bṛhaspatiṃ sarvagaṇaṃ svastaye svastaya ādityāso bhavantu naḥ //
children.translated_text: <s>Bṛhaspati</s> with all his hosts for well-being; may the <s>Ādityas</s> be for our well-being.

children.text: viśve devā no adyā svastaye vaiśvānaro vasurāgniḥ svastaye /
children.translated_text: May all the gods [grant us] well-being today; may <s>Agni Vaiśvānara</s>, the beneficent, [grant] well-being;

children.text: devā avantvṛbhavaḥ svastaye svasti no rudraḥ pātvaṃhasaḥ //
children.translated_text: may the gods, the <s>Ṛbhus</s>, [grant] well-being; may <s>Rudra</s> protect us from sin for well-being.

children.text: svasti naḥ paśyāsu dhanvasu svastyapsu vrajane svarvataḥ /
children.translated_text: Well-being to us in pastures and in deserts, well-being in waters, well-being in cattle-journeys and in heaven,

children.text: svasti naḥ pathyākṛteṣu yoniṣu svasti rāye manuto dadhātu naḥ //
children.translated_text: well-being to us in paths that are rightly made, in [our] dwelling places; may <s>Manu</s> establish well-being and wealth for us.

children.text: trātāramindraṃ, mā te asyāṃ, vina indra, mṛgo na bhīmastaṃ, śaṃyorāvṛṇīmaha iti daśāhutayaḥ // ManGS_2,15.6 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Indra</s> the protector,' 'Let not this [evil],' 'Without <s>Indra</s>,' 'Terrible like a wild beast,' 'We choose the blessing'—these are the ten oblations. // ManGS_2,15.6 //
The rest is the same beginning with the <s>jaya</s> (victory oblations). // ManGS_2,15.7 //
Thus ends the fifteenth <s>khaṇḍa</s> (chapter) in the second <s>puruṣa</s> (book) //15//
Sixteenth <s>khaṇḍa</s> (chapter)

children.text: sarpebhyo bibhyat śrāvaṇyāṃ tūṣaṇīṃ bhaumamekakapālaṃśrapayitvākṣatasaktūn piṣṭvā svakṛta iriṇe darbhānāstīryācyutāya dhruvāya bhaumāya svāheti juhoti // ManGS_2,16.1 //
children.translated_text: One who fears serpents, on the full-moon day of <s>Śrāvaṇa</s>, having silently cooked a single-kapāla cake of ground [grain] for [the deity of] the earth, having ground unhusked rice and flour, in a self-made barren spot, having spread <s>darbha</s> grass, he offers [saying] 'To the Unfaltering, the Firm, the Earthly one, <s>svāhā</s>' // ManGS_2,16.1 //

children.text: samīci nāmāsīti paryāyairupatiṣṭhate pratidiśaṃ dvābhyāṃ madhye // ManGS_2,16.2 //
children.translated_text: He worships with [the verse] 'samīcī nāmāsi' (you are called the convergent) in succession, two in each direction and [one] in the middle // ManGS_2,16.2 //
He carries the <s>sarpabali</s> (serpent offering) of unhusked rice and flour — 'to <s>Īśāna</s>' according to some —
'You are a serpent; you are the lord of serpents; in you abide all serpents /

children.text: balihāro 'stu sarpāṇāṃ namo astuṣurmāririṣurmāhiṃsiṣurmādāṃ si sarpāḥ //
children.translated_text: May this offering be for the serpents; salutation to them; may they not injure us, may they not harm us, may they not bite us, O serpents! //

children.text: māno agne visṛjo adhāyā viṣyave ripave ducchunāyai /
children.translated_text: Do not release us, O <s>Agni</s>, to the fanged one, to the hostile one, to the ill-omened one /

children.text: mā datvate daśate mādate no mā rīṣate sahasāvanparādāḥ //
children.translated_text: May the biting one not bite us, may the stinging one not sting us, may the devouring one not devour us; do not hand us over by force! //
You are a serpent; you are the lord of serpents; with a jewel you protect humans, with a cake [you protect] serpents //

children.text: tvayi santaṃ mayi santa mākṣiṣurmārīriṣurmā hiṃsiṣu mā dāṅkṣu sarpāḥ //
children.translated_text: Being present in you, being present in me — may they not crush us, may they not injure us, may they not harm us, may they not bite us, O serpents! //

children.text: namo astu sarpebhya iti tisṛbhiśca // ManGS_2,16.3 //
children.translated_text: 'Namo astu sarpebhyaḥ' (salutation to the serpents) — and with three [more verses] // ManGS_2,16.3 //

children.text: dhruvāmuṃ te paridadāmīti sarvāmātyānnāmagrāhamātmānaṃ ca // ManGS_2,16.4 //
children.translated_text: 'O Firm One, I entrust this one to you' — [naming] all ministers by name and oneself // ManGS_2,16.4 //

children.text: etena dharmeṇa caturo māsānsarpabaliṃhṛtvā viramati // ManGS_2,16.5 //
children.translated_text: Having carried the <s>sarpabali</s> (serpent offering) for four months according to this observance, he stops // ManGS_2,16.5 //
Even silently, the small [offering] with washed hands // ManGS_2,16.6 //
Thus ends the sixteenth <s>khaṇḍa</s> (chapter) in the second [book] //16//
Seventeenth <s>khaṇḍa</s> (chapter)

children.text: ayūthike bhayārtte kapote gṛhān praviṣṭe tasyājnau padaṃ dṛśyeta dadhāni sakatuṣu ghṛte vā devāḥ kapota iti pratyṛcaṃ japejjuhuyādvā devāḥ kapota iṣito yadicchandūto nirṛtyā idamājagāma /
children.translated_text: When a pigeon, stray from its flock, enters the house in distress, and its footprint is seen on the ashes — having placed curds in vessels or ghee — 'O gods, the pigeon' — he should recite verse by verse or offer oblations: 'O gods, the pigeon, sent forth, if as a messenger of <s>Nirṛti</s> (goddess of destruction) it has come here /

children.text: tasmā arcāma kṛṣṇavāma niṣkṛtiṃ śaṃ no astu dvipade śaṃ catuṣpade //
children.translated_text: Let us honor it, let us make an atonement of dark [offerings]; may there be well-being for our bipeds and quadrupeds //

children.text:
śivaḥ kapota iṣito no astvanāgā devāḥ śakuno gṛheṣu
agnirhi vipro juṣatāṃ havirnaḥ parihetiḥ pakṣiṇo no vṛṇāktu //
children.translated_text: May the pigeon sent to us be auspicious, may the bird be harmless in our houses, O gods; may <s>Agni</s> the wise be pleased with our oblation; may the winged missile spare us //

children.text: hetiḥ pakṣiṇī na dabhātyasmānāṣṭyāṃ padaṃ kṛṇute agnidhāne /
children.translated_text: The winged missile does not harm us; it makes its mark on the fire-altar /

children.text: saṃ no gobhyaśca puruṣebhyaścāstu māno hiṃsīdiha devāḥ kapotaḥ //
children.translated_text: May it be well for our cattle and our people; may the pigeon not harm us here, O gods! //
What the owl says is vain; whatever mark the pigeon makes on the fire /

children.text: yasya dūtaḥ prahita eṣa etattasmai yamāya namo astu mṛtyave //
children.translated_text: He whose messenger this one has been sent — to that <s>Yama</s>, salutation to Death! //

children.text: ṛcā kapotaṃ nudata pramodamiṣaṃ madantaḥ pari gāṃ nayadhvam /
children.translated_text: Drive away the pigeon with a verse; rejoicing, enjoying the offering, lead the cow around /

children.text: saṃyopayanto duritāni viśvā hitvā na ūrjaṃ prapatātpatiṣṭhaḥ //
children.translated_text: Averting all misfortunes, leaving behind strength, let it fly away to its resting place!' //
Thus // ManGS_2,17.1 //
Having taken the footprint, they carry it to the south and west // ManGS_2,17.2 //
They go together with the implements // ManGS_2,17.3 //
They deposit the footprint in a self-made barren spot, above [the ground] // ManGS_2,17.4 //

children.text: dhāmno dhāmna iti tisṛbhiḥ parogoṣṭhaṃ mārajayante // ManGS_2,17.5 //
children.translated_text: With the three [verses] 'dhāmno dhāmnaḥ' (from abode to abode), they drive away [evil] beyond the cow-pen // ManGS_2,17.5 //
They return without looking back // ManGS_2,17.6 //

children.text: agna āyūṃṣi pavase agnirṛṣiragne pavasveti pratyetya japanti // ManGS_2,17.7 //
children.translated_text: Having returned, they recite 'O <s>Agni</s>, you purify lifespans,' '<s>Agni</s> is the <s>ṛṣi</s> (seer),' 'O <s>Agni</s>, purify' // ManGS_2,17.7 //
Thus ends the seventeenth <s>khaṇḍa</s> (chapter) in the second [book] //17//
Eighteenth <s>khaṇḍa</s> (chapter)
The six-oblation [rite is performed] on the first day [of the fortnight] by one desiring a son // ManGS_2,18.1 //
Having cooked a <s>sthālīpāka</s> (oblation in a pot) in milk, from that he offers —

children.text:
brahmaṇāgniḥ saṃvidāno rakṣohā bādhātāmitaḥ /
amī vā yaste garbhaṃ durṇāmā yonimāśaye /
children.translated_text: 'May <s>Agni</s>, in accord with <s>Brahman</s>, the destroyer of <s>rākṣasas</s> (demons), drive away from here / those evil-named ones who beset your womb and lie in the womb /
Those evil-named ones who beset your womb and lie in the womb /
<s>Agni</s>, together with <s>Brahman</s>, having gone forth, has destroyed the indestructible //

children.text: yaste hantī patayantaṃ niṣatsnuṃ yaḥ sarīsṛpam /
children.translated_text: The one who strikes your [child] as it falls, the crawling one /
The one who seeks to kill the newborn — that one we destroy from here //
The one who, having deluded you with sleep and darkness, lies upon you /
The one who seeks to kill your offspring — that one we destroy from here //

children.text: ye te ghnantyapso gandharvā goṣṭhāśca ye /
children.translated_text: Those <s>gandharvas</s> who slay your [children] in the waters, and those in the cow-pens /
The flesh-eating <s>asura</s> (demon) gambler — that one we destroy from here //
The one who separates your thighs, who lies between husband and wife /
The one who defiles the womb from within — that one we destroy from here //
With unbroken egg, with mature embryo, unharmed, giving birth to living [children] /
May she give birth, may she be fruitful; may this woman have offspring! //
May <s>Viṣṇu</s> prepare the womb, may <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> fashion the forms /
May <s>Prajāpati</s> pour forth; may <s>Dhātṛ</s> place the embryo in you! //

children.text: garbhaṃ dhehi sītīvāli garbhaṃ dhehi sarasvati /
children.translated_text: Place the embryo, O <s>Sinīvālī</s>; place the embryo, O <s>Sarasvatī</s> /
May the two <s>Aśvins</s>, the divine ones, wearing lotus garlands, place the embryo in you! //
The golden fire-churning sticks which the two <s>Aśvins</s> churn /

children.text: taṃ te garbhaṃ havāmahe daśame māsi sūtave //
children.translated_text: That embryo we invoke for you, for delivery in the tenth month! //

children.text: paraṃ mṛtyo anuparehi panthāṃ yaste sva itaro devayānāt /
children.translated_text: O Death, go past on another path, one that is your own, different from the path of the gods /

children.text: cakṣuṣmate śṛṇavate te bravīmi mānaḥ prajāṃ rīriṣo mota vīrān //
children.translated_text: I speak to you who have eyes and ears — do not injure our offspring nor our heroes! //

children.text: iti dvādaśagarbhavedinyaḥ ṣaḍādyāḥ sthālīpākasya ṣaḍutarā ājyasya // ManGS_2,18.2 //
children.translated_text: Thus [these are] the twelve <s>garbhavedanī</s> (embryo-knowledge) [verses]; the first six are for the <s>sthālīpāka</s>, the latter six are for the ghee oblation // ManGS_2,18.2 //
From the <s>jaya</s> (victory oblations) onward, it is the same [as the standard procedure] // ManGS_2,18.3 //
Having cooked a <s>sthālīpāka</s> for <s>Naijameṣa</s>, as in the six-oblation [rite] —
'O <s>Naijameṣa</s>, fly away and return as one with good sons /

children.text: asyai me putrakāmāyai punarādhehi yaḥ pumān //
children.translated_text: For this woman of mine who desires a son, place again a male [child]! //
Just as this great earth, lying on her back, received the embryo /

children.text: evaṃ taṃ garbhamādhehi daśame māsi sūtave //
children.translated_text: So place that embryo [in her] for delivery in the tenth month! //
With the most excellent form of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, in this woman, in [her] womb /
Place a male son for delivery in the tenth month! //
Having prepared the <s>pākayajñas</s> (domestic sacrifices) with a single ghee [vessel] and a single [bundle of] sacrificial grass /

children.text: ekaṃ sviṣṭakṛtaṃ puryannānā satyapi daivate nānā satyapi daivate // ManGS_2,18.4 //
children.translated_text: A single <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s> (offering for completion) being offered — even when the deities are different, even when the deities are different // ManGS_2,18.4 //
Thus ends the eighteenth <s>khaṇḍa</s> (chapter) in the second <s>puruṣa</s> (book) //18//
Thus ends the section called the second <s>puruṣa</s> (book) in the <s>Maitrāyaṇīya Mānavagṛhyasūtra</s> /
And the <s>sūtra</s> is completed //
